## Schema selection terminology

Schema holds Field roots and metadata; its equality ignores schema metadata, while configurable comparison can include it. Projectable exposes a borrowed Schema, and Projection selects field IDs plus four metadata-column flags and a blob policy. These are in-memory schemas/selections, not executed read plans. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:28-35; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:178-181; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:922-926; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1147-1156; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1239-1252)

## Cache serialization vocabulary

LCE1 envelope carries a type identity and body version; CacheDecode distinguishes Hit from a reasoned Miss. CacheEntryWriter/Reader manage typed-body sections and absolute offsets, independently of the16-byte key digest. See [cache module](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md) and [format reconstruction](L3-symbols/format-spec.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:144-273; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:28-38; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:117-126)


## Weighted cache budgets

Moka and Quick are in-memory CacheBackend implementations. Their eviction weights include fixed key cost plus declared entry size; shared-buffer-aware deep traversal is a separate callback-based metric. Quick can partition a budget among shards or use a single shard, so fitting the total cache does not imply admission to one shard. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:25-47; rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:196-209; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:46-56; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:107-112; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:351-377)


## Typed cache handles

LanceCache clones and child namespaces share backend, counters and type-aware memory callbacks. WeakLanceCache preserves namespace without a strong state reference and can compute a sized value after expiry without caching it. CacheStats counts successful coalesced loads as hits and excludes loader errors; these semantics differ from a raw request success/failure counter. [Full cache surface](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:220-271; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:322-366; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:502-553; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:652-800)

## Encoded row identity and operation disposition

InlineRowIds keeps byte content and a shared lazy digest memo together so clones reuse both and replacing the wrapper does not carry an old digest into new bytes. Its digest identifies encoded content, not decoded-row equivalence. RowIdMeta chooses inline bytes or hidden-column storage. (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:27-98; rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:141-166)

The format-layer Transaction is a public protobuf wrapper; its schema-change classification is a conservative operation disposition used to decide where validation may be needed, not validation itself. It has no commit lifecycle in its local body. (rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs:16-82)


## Three version domains and manifest ownership

Dataset version is Manifest.version (with bit63 identifying a detached version), writer version is library-specific semver metadata, and data storage version is an exact ConcreteFileVersion. Treat these as separate domains. A Manifest is an in-memory snapshot with shared fragments and private cached logical offsets; its protobuf serialization is not a complete file or a commit. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:39-132; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:579-589; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:734-780)

Fragment metadata ties columns of the same physical rows to base DataFiles, ordered overlays, optional deletion and inline/column lineage. Every-file operations must account for overlays; lineage lookup intentionally uses base files only. These metadata rules now connect the flag policy to manifest decoding and shallow cloning; dataset IO and transaction publication are still untraced. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:519-558; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:589-725; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:248-320; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1045-1079)


## Three distinct coverage domains

Index fragment_bitmap tracks fragment IDs; overlay bitmaps track physical offsets within a fragment; key-existence Bloom data tracks encoded join keys for conflict detection. They cannot substitute for one another. Unknown index coverage is None, sparse overlay coverage is positional per field, and a Bloom overlap is only a possible key conflict. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:62-67; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:65-74; rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:175-212)

Covered index fields are dependencies whose values are carried with results; keyed fields decide which search the index can answer. Physical metadata currently validates a suffix representation. The protobuf's future independent-covering feature must not be assumed implemented by that validator. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:36-51; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:160-247; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:86-97)


## File-version request, identity and footer

Caller Stable/Next selectors resolve to exact2.2/2.3 in this snapshot. Persisted identities have no ordering; use explicit capabilities instead of comparing release numbers. V2.0 standard footer is(0,3), embedded footer and DataFile metadata are(2,0), while manifest string is2.0. These spellings describe the same exact identity. Footer-only detection reads8 bytes and does not certify a valid complete file. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60)

Overlay staleness is a metadata-derived conservative exclusion set: union newer changes to indexed dependency fields or their ancestors/descendants, then consumers must re-evaluate affected rows. This differs from resolving the newest value and from deleting rows; the helper only returns/accumulates physical offset sets. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:4-13; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:35-176)


## Positional lineage glossary

- **RowDatasetVersionRun / Sequence:** one dataset version per positional span, stored as runs aligned with row-ID order. Numeric span coordinates are not stable row IDs; consumers use cumulative lengths. [Version module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:272-311)
- **SpilledRowLineage:** preloaded row IDs/creation/update sequences keyed by fragment ID, allowing synchronous manifest preparation to preserve column-stored lineage. Loading itself remains a caller responsibility. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:750-769)
- **HoleRuns:** maximal missing-offset runs plus present-count prefixes, supporting offset-to-ordinal rank and inverse selection. It represents holes in a row-ID segment, not dataset-version runs or deletion-file IO. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:132-190)


## Row-ID representation terms

- **Bitmap:** internal presence bits indexed LSB first within each byte; logical length is separate from byte capacity. Constructors normalize padding, raw construction does not. The schema comment disagrees on bit order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-105; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)
- **EncodedU64Array:** owned U16/U32 relative offsets plus a base or plain U64 values; compressed does not imply sorted. Wire packed integers are little-endian. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-26; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-230)
- **Range folding:** decoder merges adjacency and groups ascending separated ranges through the segment helper; sequence writer expands the compact Ranges form back into plain wire Range arms. This changes in-memory representation without adding a protobuf arm. [Codec overview](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:60-96; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-255; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:376-398)


## Segment coordinates and scan state

- **U64Segment:** one of six in-memory representations of an intended distinct u64 sequence. Numeric values, present ordinals and enclosing numeric bounds are separate coordinates. Selection chooses five forms; compact Ranges comes from explicit range grouping/bitmap conversion. [Module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:16-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:196-299)
- **SegmentCursor / SegmentCursorState:** a public borrowed segment reader and its crate-visible bitmap byte/rank state. The wrapper fixes the source; reusable state alone does not. Dense expansion batches contiguous set-bit runs, while selection indices count present values. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)


## Row-ID sequences and ordinal selection

RowIdSequence preserves fragment row order across segments. Stable numeric IDs, ordinal positions and tree-map set membership are distinct: set conversion discards order, while masks translate selected IDs back into ordinal ranges. Public checked construction rejects duplicates within one input; raw range/slice conversions and extend do not enforce table-wide uniqueness. [Sequence analysis](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:39-52; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:209-265; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:302-319; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-797; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905)

RowIdSeqSlice is a borrowed positional view. RowIdSequenceCursor instead owns scan counters without a source lifetime: it rewinds for decreasing requests and resets segment state at boundaries, but callers must keep its sequence stable across calls. Internal selection clips at EOF; the public ReadBatchParams adapter has separate bounds/error behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:54-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:456-494; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:559-592; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:908-943; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:1055-1127)



## Creation lineage during transaction preparation

Creation version records first appearance; last-update version records the commit changing values. The reviewed transaction helper resolves stable IDs back to source physical offsets, preserves known creation versions, falls back to1 for unavailable creation of a found source, and stamps new IDs with the supplied commit version. Writer-placed lineage means row-ID Column or creation-version Column; it is a metadata predicate, not a provenance check. [Table details](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) and [local scenario](L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) separate these synchronous metadata mutations from the separately documented [IO](L3-symbols/protocol-io.md) and [publication](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md) protocols. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:21-79; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:258-295)




## Transaction intent and one-attempt preparation

A Transaction stores read_version,UUID,Operation,optional tag and shared string properties. An Operation names one of16 change kinds with typed payloads. PreparedIndices separately carries current-attempt original/prepared index metadata and fragment-reuse intent; it is not persisted by these containers. Retry/conflict/publication behavior is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). [Transaction API](L1-modules/rust-lance-table-transactions.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/builder.rs:12-25; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:37-262; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:4-18; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:44-100)

CoverageIdentity means UUID plus optional fragment bitmap, with other index metadata excluded from equality. ReadVersionState means borrowed manifest/index evidence from a transaction's fixed read version; it carries no runtime check that the pair matches. UpdatedFragmentOffsets means per-fragment physical offset bitmaps for partial column-update lineage. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:66-106; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:277-282)




## Equality versus conflict compatibility

Operation equality compares represented intent; different operation kinds always differ. Separate metadata predicates compare config upserts/deletes or table/schema/field metadata scopes. Their bool results are consumed by the commit conflict resolver, whose directional matrix is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). Durable commit-outcome identity uses protobuf forms in the inspected path, not these in-memory payload comparisons. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:18-29; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:863-991; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2347-2360; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:261-301)




## Operation pre-validation

Pre-validation checks operation shape against an optional current manifest. It is synchronous metadata inspection with no storage IO; its success does not certify physical files, schema completeness in modern formats or transaction compatibility. Merge field-binding protection and a separate base-file rewrite detector serve different purposes: binding safety versus latest-version stamping. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:377-724; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:825-1044; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1209-1268)




## Durable transaction representation

Operation intent converts to a generated protobuf transaction before storage. Rust optional-empty states and transient rewrite metadata may disappear; unknown update-mode values decode as row rewrite, and empty rewrite groups take a legacy fallback. Therefore in-memory equality, decoded operation equality and persisted protobuf identity are distinct contracts. Byte storage/outcome recovery is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:151-184; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:244-283; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:408-422; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:555-569; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:261-301)




## Stored index provenance versus live coverage

An index segment's stored fragment bitmap can name retired source fragments, while history maps their rows to later destinations. Unknown coverage (None), known empty coverage and known retired provenance have different retention behavior. TaggedLineage separates stored coverage membership from whether history is walkable; known-empty destination lists differ from unknown lineage. These distinctions drive invalidation and retention, with implementation navigation in the [index protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-index.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:4-107; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:426-451; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:593-645; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:2334-2340; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:2412-2548)


## Encoder orchestration glossary

A field encoder buffers a logical Arrow field and may emit several physical columns. A field strategy selects it before data; an array strategy selects a page encoder. EncodeTask produces one page asynchronously. OutOfLineBuffers reserves absolute padded positions but retains unpadded payloads; actual writers must implement the reservation. FieldEncodingContext carries the complete recursive strategy and root metadata. The in-memory encode_batch helper is a separate test/IPC path with sequential polling and unpadded appends. [Encoding module](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:56-73; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:117-233; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:288-322; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:398-501)


## Decoder facade glossary

Scheduling selects byte ranges and produces page messages; decoding materializes Arrow arrays through tasks. Array and structural message grammars are distinct. A ReadBatchTask carries a future plus expected row count. Structural byte targets adapt using reported decoded size and can overshoot; array i32-offset limits are a separate mechanism. RequestBatch aggregates I/O calls while preserving each caller's buffer order. [Module contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1542-1558; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1636-1734; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2089-2199; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2863-3064)


## Primitive index and value terms

A mini-block has distinct byte, top-level-row and leaf-value coordinates. A trailer begins a row continued in the next block; that next block has a preamble. Constant pages retain one scalar plus repetition/definition levels, then materialize selected leaf positions. Dictionary normalization moves null dictionary entries into key validity before encoding; physical null-key repair prevents invalid hidden indices when validity is removed. [Helper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/chunk_index.rs:185-343; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/constant.rs:341-492; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/dict.rs:30-170)


## Blob decode view and representation

Original BlobLayout stores position/size descriptions plus same-file payload buffers; descriptor-only reads and binary materialization use separate cache views. Blob-v2 prepared records become kind/position/size/blob_id/blob_uri descriptors, with sidecar/URI handling outside this encoder. A payload shard is a byte-targeted group of original Blob reads, distinct from dataset fragments or MemWAL shards;32MiB is a target that can be exceeded. [Blob contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:31-465; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:262-432; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:4708-4725)


## Fixed slots and map entries

A fixed-size-list dimension gives the number of child slots per outer row. Null outer rows still reserve those slots; variable-size descendants under them can be cleared with a garbage mask. Map entries are Struct key/value rows whose offsets and parent validity are reconstructed through rep/def layers. The current complex FSL path requires immediate Struct children, while Map requires unsorted entries and a nonnullable key. [Nested wrapper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). # Lance engine orientation

> Refresh 2026-10-11, `4ac2f7c88be1ea2ab2c0fbb61d02238883fc18b9`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-11.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

> Refresh 2026-10-09, `db684d1f0726c00b6defb7963a604a7719e82b5a`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-09.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

> Refresh 2026-10-07, `84d1681e07af565837f2d97e72ff1b8b040cd15c`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-07.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

**Navigation and contracts; source access is expected.** Start here, choose a path, and open its ordered source set. Deep format details live in the [format contract](L3-symbols/format-spec.md), terminology in the [engine glossary](L0-glossary.md), and exact retained declarations in the [frozen symbol snapshot](L3-symbols/symbol-index.md). [Scope and trust](V21-PROTOCOL.md).

## Architecture and state ownership

Lance presents a versioned Dataset over immutable data files and versioned metadata. A fragment groups physical columns for the same rows; its manifest entry carries deletion, overlay and lineage metadata. A Dataset handle owns a manifest snapshot plus stores, commit handler and session/cache handles. Publishing a new manifest makes a mutation visible; finishing a data file alone does not publish a dataset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-87; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-572; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:1-264)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  API[Dataset / Scanner / write and index builders] --> Plan[Scan planning and execution nodes]
  API --> Tx[Transaction preparation and commit]
  Plan --> Index[Scalar / vector / full-text indices]
  Plan --> Fragment[Fragment reads and row identity]
  Fragment --> File[lance-file exact-version readers]
  API --> Writer[Fragment / file writers]
  Writer --> File
  File --> Encoding[lance-encoding page and buffer mechanisms]
  File --> IO[lance-io stores and scheduled reads]
  Tx --> Table[lance-table manifests, operations and conflicts]
  Table --> Publish[CommitHandler publication]
  Publish --> IO
  Index --> IO
  Core[lance-core schemas, errors and common data structures] --> API
  Core --> Table
  Protos[Handwritten protobuf schemas] --> Table
  Protos --> File
```

The arrows identify ownership/call boundaries rather than a claim that every request crosses every box. Scanner creates a physical plan; the DataFusion adapter executes it and returns a RecordBatch stream. Encoding describes pages and schedules their bytes through an I/O seam; it does not commit Dataset versions. Index creation writes index state before committing CreateIndex metadata. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2999-3015; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-134; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:696-743)

## Read path

**Entry:** `dataset.scan().try_into_stream().await?`. The stream must be consumed to execute reads. This is a trace of the public Rust path; it is not a command that was run during KB work.

1. `Dataset::scan` clones the snapshot into `Scanner`. Configure projection/filter/vector/limit before planning. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1688-1705)
2. `Scanner::create_plan_impl` validates options, resolves full-text/query filters, chooses vector, full-text, MinHash or filtered read source, and adds filtering, ordering, limit and final projection. Scalar index use is conditioned on prefiltering or absence of nearest search. Conflicting search modes error. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3633-3801)
3. `try_into_stream` passes the plan, batch size and statistics callback to `execute_plan`. Multiple output partitions are merged with order preservation when ordering exists; execution starts at partition 0 of that final plan. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2999-3015; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)
4. The selected source reads fragment metadata/deletions/lineage and reaches exact-version file readers. File open loads footer/global/column metadata; prepared reads schedule pages, decode selected values and materialize batches. The local contract is in the [frozen shared-reader record](L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs.md); source ranges are rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:732-1020. No guarantee is made that every query reads every column or uses an index.

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1688-1705` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2999-3042,3633-3801` → `rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761` → `rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:732-1020`. For a particular scan operator, follow the scanner's selected source rather than opening all execution nodes.

## Write path

**Entry:** `Dataset::write(reader, destination, Some(params)).await?`.

1. `Dataset::write` constructs `InsertBuilder`, applies params and calls `execute_stream`; the input reader is converted into stream/schema. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:951-980; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-120)
2. Resolve destination/store/version, validate the write, resolve target bases and write fragments. A fixed data filename combined with target bases is rejected. `execute_uncommitted` stops after building a transaction: data objects may exist, but no manifest has been published. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:144-265)
3. Create and overwrite produce `Operation::Overwrite`; append produces `Operation::Append`. The transaction's read version comes from the destination snapshot or 0 for a new destination. File assembly/flush belongs to the fragment writer, and its exact bytes to the selected file-version writer. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:267-315; rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1734-1840)
4. `do_commit` configures `CommitBuilder`. Existing datasets use the retrying transaction path (or the explicitly selected detached path); new datasets use `commit_new_dataset`. Detached new-dataset creation is rejected; detached commit cannot use V1 manifest naming. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:148-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)
5. Successful publication returns a Dataset carrying the committed manifest/location and caches. Data-file existence is not commit evidence; error/outcome recovery belongs to `io/commit.rs`. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:516-572; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:273-301)

**Ordered initial read set (5 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:951-980` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-315` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1734-1840` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:301-572` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1682-1941`. The exact persisted manifest contract is already available through the [frozen table I/O record](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs.md).

## Compaction path

**Entry:** `compact_files(&mut dataset, options, remap_options).await?`.

1. Construct and run the compaction planner. Reject eager index remapping on a tagged fragment-reuse history. No planned tasks means no new committed version. Execute planned rewrites with bounded concurrency and collect successful results. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152)
2. Each rewrite validates its target exact file version, refreshes required fragment statistics and chooses binary-copy or scan/re-encode. A forced binary-copy request cannot silently fall back. Capture old physical row addresses only when a consumer needs remapping; stable row IDs use their own lineage. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2494-2569; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2693-2789)
3. `commit_compaction` validates tagged-history/remap requirements and takes the **minimum RewriteResult.read_version**, so conflicts since task planning remain visible even if the caller opened a newer Dataset handle. Address-style outputs reserve fragment IDs; remap indices now or produce deferred fragment-reuse metadata according to the selected protocol. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3227-3337)
4. Commit a Rewrite operation through Dataset's normal commit boundary. Old files are not made safe to delete merely by writing replacements; retain manifest/version retention policy. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3662-3693; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:74-123)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152,2494-2789,3227-3337,3662-3693` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1682-1941` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1546-1813,2973-3229` → [frozen manifest application](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs.md). Split copy mechanics or a specific index remapper into a separate task instead of expanding this read set without bound.

## Index build and query path

**Entry:** `DatasetIndexExt::create_index` / `create_index_builder`; query through Scanner.

1. The Dataset extension constructs `CreateIndexBuilder`; optional name and replace settings are applied before awaiting it. The builder validates one-column admission and reserves names against all stored indices, including unsupported ones. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2456-2490; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:176-225)
2. Build/train through the selected scalar/vector index implementation; `execute_uncommitted` yields metadata without publication. Multi-segment FM-Index construction has a separate atomic multi-index path. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:176-225; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:696-713)
3. On replacement, collect same-name metadata to remove, then commit CreateIndex with newly built metadata. Reload the committed index by UUID so the return value reflects commit-time changes; missing UUID after commit errors. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:706-743)
4. Scanner later selects index-backed or scan-backed sources from query/filter options. Data not covered by an index must be accounted for by that query path; never equate a stored index bitmap with all current rows. The distinctions are in the [frozen index metadata contract](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3716-3801)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/index.rs:2456-2490` → `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:176-225,696-743` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3716-3801` → [frozen index metadata](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). Concrete scalar/IVF-PQ implementation choices belong to the M2 index Module Map, not an assumed universal build pipeline.

## Essential distinctions

- File format version, Dataset manifest version, per-row creation/update version and index version are different domains. Never compare them interchangeably. [Exact version matrix](L3-symbols/format-spec.md); [glossary](L0-glossary.md).
- Stable logical row IDs differ from physical `(fragment_id, offset)` addresses; compaction changes physical addresses. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:6-79; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81)
- Declaration in a protobuf union does not establish acceptance in every exact file version. Reader grammar and writer selection are independent checks. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:99-119; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:99-127)
- Stable format compatibility is durable; unstable formats may change; frozen legacy paths are not new-feature extension points. (AGENTS.md:5-20)

This orientation completes M1's architecture and four public paths. Detailed subsystem/API contracts and navigation tests remain independently tracked in M2–M4; no build or runtime execution is claimed.

## Development entry

Choose a task in the [ordered navigation index](L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md), then read its contract and bounded implementation set. API-only questions start at [public contracts and bindings](L3-symbols/public-api.md).

## Dependencies and extension boundaries

ANN imports table identity, table index metadata, and index metric types; filtered read imports table identity; index imports protobuf Any and historical index details. These are schema type dependencies. Build-time generators, crate boundaries, and runtime registrations remain pending. (protos/ann.proto:8-10; protos/ann.proto:92-95; protos/filtered_read.proto:8-8; protos/index.proto:8-9)

Add new detail kinds in index.proto; do not relocate existing lance.table types solely for naming consistency because serialized identities matter. Extending existing historical messages is explicitly allowed where needed. The explanatory comment abbreviates the new namespace as lance.index, but the actual package is lance.index.pb. (protos/index_old.proto:8-17; protos/index.proto:6-6)

There are no environment-variable declarations or Cargo feature definitions in the reviewed schema bodies. Manifest feature requirements occur as explicit numeric contracts: overlays need 64, and hidden column lineage needs 2048. Actual supported flags, their stability, and read/write gates must be established from table and Rust code. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:19-27; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51)

Decoder failure modes are not executable in these files. Notable required validations include MinHash field ranges before allocation, unknown signature-version rejection, and exact lineage column cardinality. (protos/index.proto:332-382; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-309)

Table imports Any, Timestamp, shared file schema and publicly re-exports fragment metadata. Transaction imports file/table/Any. file2 imports Any and Empty but only uses Empty in declarations; old encoding schema imports Empty for plain column encoding. The new encoding schema has no imports. These are schema dependencies, not a reconstructed Cargo dependency graph. ## Responsibility and runtime values

The module copies complete encoded pages into an ordinary output file, relocating buffer offsets and priorities and regenerating metadata/footer. It does not publish a Dataset transaction, choose a fallback, reserve Blob IDs or own source storage. EncodedFileInput holds a scheduler and optional expected physical row count; the expectation is checked later. DataFilePart additionally retains normalized schema, cached metadata and optional Blob lease/target. Neither object pins an ETag/hash or rechecks immutability during copying. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:4-8; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:60-127; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:808-1048; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1185-1193)

BlobTargetId is an arbitrary Arc string compared by value. It is not persisted and does not establish Dataset/base/object-store authority. FileConcatTarget stores an exact version, Arc schema and optional target identity. FileConcatResult separates Written, Reused(index, output metadata) and Unsupported(reason); malformed/missing inputs instead return Err. All public declarations and fields, private helpers and exact generic bounds are cataloged below. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:39-58; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:513-538; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:558-691)

## Entry paths and validation order

1. Ordinary concat_files rejects empty inputs, concurrently reads raw metadata, then returns LegacyVersion if the target or any input is V1. It finalizes all current metadata before shared compatibility. IO/metadata errors can precede the legacy result. Ordinary target Blob fields are unsupported. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:697-725; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1091-1131)
2. DataFilePart::open first checks lease shape, reads full metadata and reconstructs anonymous Blob descriptor children, checks expected rows, rejects Blob v1, validates rectangular metadata and compares normalized/footer counts. Blob v2 descriptor validation happens before requiring a target ID. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:140-225)
3. concat_data_file_parts rejects empty input, compares optional target identities for every part, then sorts declared leases and rejects overlap. It borrows already validated metadata/schema without reopening or checking Blob descriptors again. Touching leases are legal. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1151-1193)
4. Shared preparation rejects read_batch_bytes=0, then checks compatibility and total-row overflow. A single ordinary input is reused with no output factory or writer-option use. Part mode always writes a new file after successful validation, including one part. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:929-968)

| Compatibility sequence | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected row count differs | InvalidInput with path/actual/expected |
| Exact version differs | Unsupported VersionMismatch |
| Schema differs from full target or descriptor-projected target | Unsupported SchemaMismatch |
| External metadata validation fails or normalized rows differ from footer | CorruptFile |
| More than one global buffer | Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers |
| Column count differs from first input | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(None) |
| Any column-level buffers | Unsupported ColumnBuffers |
| Physical column index differs | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(Some(index)) |
| Serialized column-level encoding differs | Unsupported ColumnEncodingMismatch |

Order is per input after baseline encoding serialization. Column encodings compare protobuf Any bytes; page encodings and page counts may differ. These checks precede the output factory, but page ranges and IO response lengths are checked later. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:693-806)

## Blob schema and descriptor boundary

Footer reconstruction finds top-level consecutive runs matching anonymous descriptor children by ID=-1,parent=-1,name,logical type and empty children. It drains those runs and attaches them to childless Blob nodes in preorder. It does not compare child nullability/metadata/encoding, require all missing nodes be repaired or reject unconsumed queue entries. This is a local interpretation of existing footer metadata, not a migration or new persisted format. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:232-302)

Descriptor validation requires distinct nonnegative Blob field IDs, constructs exact physical-column projection, then opens another FileReader with no cache and streams8192 rows/readahead4. Thus Blob part opening can read metadata twice. It validates decoded descriptor arrays; managed Blob payloads are not loaded here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:316-377)

| Selected nonnull descriptor kind | Required here | Outside this check |
|---|---|---|
| Inline | size must equal0 | position and ID |
| Packed | lease present and ID contained | payload existence, range bounds, size, repeated IDs |
| Dedicated | lease membership and position0 | payload existence and complete-file size |
| External | recognized kind only | URI, base authority, offset and size |

Unknown kinds propagate BlobKind conversion error. Missing named kind/position/size/blob_id fields are CorruptFile; incorrect Arrow types can panic at downcasts. Descriptor child nulls have no separate guard, and blob_uri is not inspected. Lease shape requires1<=start<end, independently of descriptor content. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:304-314; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:379-457; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:601-649)

Struct validity intersects row selection; List/LargeList expand only selected valid parents into child offset ranges. Other containers receive no recursive branch here. A malformed Arrow array/selection can panic through indexing/casts; this function relies on typed decoded arrays. Whole leases are checked for overlap even for non-Blob parts that merely carry unused ranges. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:458-511; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1165-1183; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1519-1556)

## Copying, memory and failure lifecycle

Inputs and physical columns are processed sequentially. Consecutive complete pages are batched by summed payload bytes; the default16MiB threshold is soft because the first page is admitted even when larger. Zero-length buffers consume no read result but still call the writer's empty external-buffer path. Offsets and sums use checked arithmetic; actual range<=EOF is delegated to IO. The scheduler may coalesce/split requests internally, so one submit_request is not a proven single backend read. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:540-556; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:808-905)

Each positive buffer response must match its recorded length exactly. New PageInfo preserves rows and encoding, replaces physical offsets and checked-adds prior input row count to priority. Priority overflow and extra-response errors occur after potential writes. Metadata for all inputs and all output pages is retained even though payload reads are batched. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:906-928; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:950-1024; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1096-1130)

V2_0 structural header columns copy only until output pages exist, then normalize the first header page to total rows,priority0 and truncate to one. Other current versions copy every column and need no final page adjustment. Column-level encoding comes from the first input. An empty external-buffer write aligns the schema descriptor before initialize_with_external_columns and normal finish. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:975-1034; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:230-276; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:84-132)

The explicit abort runs only for errors inside the copy/finalize/finish async block. Factory and lazy-writer-construction failures occur before that block; cancellation does not reach its error match. Abort returns no Result at this boundary, so no successful deletion/durable rollback is established. A reused or unsupported result never invokes the output factory. Source and output object identity separation is not checked here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:955-969; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1038-1048; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:261-269)

## Dependencies and caller seam

Core supplies Schema/Field/Blob conventions, errors and cache; Arrow arrays expose descriptor/null/offset structure; lance-encoding provides normalized ColumnInfo/PageInfo and decoder plugins; lance-io provides schedulers, row selectors and writer trait; prost/prost-types provide exact encoding comparison. The std ordered collections make field-ID maps and lease/schema reconstruction deterministic locally, while futures drives concurrent metadata reads and streaming descriptors. No new feature flag or environment variable is defined. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:10-37; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:316-377; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:693-725; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1096-1101)

A narrowly inspected Dataset wrapper opens all parts, derives target path/store/ID, calls concat with default options, treats Reused as Internal, maps version/schema/other unsupported reasons to distinct errors and returns DataFile with output size. Its loader checks stored size before opening parts with expected rows and lease; its target ID builder uses base:id or primary plus filename. These are observed integration snippets, not full Dataset authority/recovery analysis. ## Ownership and configuration

FileWriter<M: ManifestProvider + Send + Sync> owns a Box<dyn Writer>, Schema, signed next batch ID, ordinary page table, cumulative metadata and optional statistics collector. Only object_writer is public; the provider is a PhantomData marker, not a runtime instance. The writer has no closed flag, custom Drop, abort guard or ownership-consuming finish. Replacing the public writer does not reset stored state. The ignored example is obsolete: actual calls are try_new, write with a slice, and async finish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:66-87; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:98-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:255-290)

FileWriterOptions has one field: collect_stats_for_fields. None selects every schema ID; Some(empty) disables statistics; nonempty IDs are projected with include_all_children=true before supported fields become collector builders. Unknown IDs are not explicitly rejected here. The collector may return None even after a nonempty request. The fully analyzed support predicate accepts Boolean, signed/unsigned integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, UTF8/Binary with both offset widths and Decimal128; it excludes several types that collect_statistics can independently dispatch, including timestamps, duration, dictionary and fixed binary. Do not equate dispatcher support with automatic collection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:89-137; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:463-478; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:550-633)

try_new creates the target object before constructing local state. with_object_writer accepts an arbitrary writer position and supplied schema without validation or dictionary hydration. There is no local environment variable, version selector, compression setting or memory budget. Store creation/overwrite policy and backend cleanup are delegated and still require IO implementation analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:99-137)

## Per-call state transitions

| Stage | Effects and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| Empty input slice | Returns Ok without validation, stats, IO, flush or counter changes |
| Validate every input batch | Convert Arrow schema; compare with stored schema ignoring declared nullability, metadata, field IDs and dictionary contents; recursively reject actual nulls in stored nonnullable fields |
| Collect stats | One row per supported selected field for the entire slice; mutates builders before writes |
| Write roots sequentially | Clone schema fields, find batch columns by name, recursively encode all arrays at current batch ID; earlier page entries and bytes survive later failure |
| Append logical length | Unchecked i32 row casts/sum and cumulative offset mutation |
| Flush | Polls in-flight writer requests before caller regains control; a failure leaves cumulative metadata advanced |
| Advance batch ID | Happens only after successful flush |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:166-236. A single call with several batches creates one stored batch. A nonempty slice containing a zero-row batch still traverses encoding and advances the batch ID on success; it is not the empty-slice no-op. The zero-row UTF8 test explicitly reopens batch0. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:985-1014)

Schema comparison retains normal ordered name/logical-type/child matching, with the shared blob-child comparison exception inherited from Field. Recursive nullability checks zip field children with ArrayData child_data and inspect physical null counts without ancestor masks or list-child logical-span slicing. They do not independently validate counts; normal schema comparison occurs first. Dictionary equality is assumed by a comment to have been checked earlier, but this writer performs no comparison or unification. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:83-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:423-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:978-1028; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:144-199)

Statistics traversal uses a LIFO stack: roots and struct children are visited in reverse schema order, structs are expanded without emitting their own node, and other nested types are skipped with descendants. It uses borrowed arrays, allocates per-field vectors and does no task spawning or ancestor-validity combination. Collector output ordering instead follows its BTreeMap by original field ID. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:654-692; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:612-670)

## Page grammar and recursive writes

```text
one nonempty write(slice)
+-- scalar/null root -> one (field ID, batch ID) PageInfo
+-- struct root
|   `-- each child recursively; no parent payload/validity page
+-- list root
|   +-- parent Int32 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
|   `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
`-- large-list root
    +-- parent Int64 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
    `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
```

Dispatch uses the first actual array DataType. Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary adapters assert the corresponding field.encoding rather than return a validation error. Arrays are processed sequentially; boxed async recursion does not spawn a task. Unsupported final match returns Schema error. The earlier fixed-stride guard already covers FixedSizeList/FixedSizeBinary, so the later explicit arm adds no extra support. The binary-like predicate includes view types; the concrete legacy BinaryEncoder rejects views as InvalidInput and does not normalize them. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:292-391; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:406-459; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105)

| Adapter | Stored position and length | Additional contract |
|---|---|---|
| Null | Current cursor; logical row count | No payload or encoding-tag check |
| Plain | Encoder return at value bytes; logical elements | Assert Plain and nonempty input; validity is delegated to frozen codec semantics |
| Binary | Offset table after payload; logical elements | Assert VarBinary; absolute i64 offsets rather than a separate validity bitmap |
| Dictionary | Key bytes; logical keys | Values come from stored schema at footer time, not batch arrays |
| Struct | No parent page | Assert child count, find children by name and recurse; no parent validity |
| List/LargeList | Parent offset bytes; rows+1 | Normalize selected child spans; recursively write children[0]; no parent validity |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-586; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-87. PageInfo length is not encoded byte length. Counts and offsets use unchecked casts/sums; encoding errors may occur after bytes are written but before the current page entry is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

List writers retain each sliced values array from first through final offset, excluding outside tails but retaining storage inside null-list spans. They append initial zero and normalized offsets using usize arithmetic, then cast to i32/i64. Builder capacity is rows although rows+1 positions are appended. Position bytes/table entry precede child writes, so child failure leaves partial output. children[0] is unchecked, and no list validity is persisted. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:491-586)

## Footer, provider and shutdown

```text
ordinary data pages, written across calls
`-- finish()
    +-- ordinary dense PageTable, minimum schema field ID
    +-- optional statistics arrays and separate PageTable at batch 0
    +-- schema dictionary values; update stored offset/length metadata
    +-- M::store_schema -> optional schema/manifest position
    +-- u32 LE framed Metadata protobuf
    +-- i64 LE metadata position, i16 LE 0, i16 LE 2, "LANC"
    `-- Writer::shutdown -> authoritative size_bytes
```

The minimum schema field ID includes struct roots and is unwrapped; an empty schema panics. A nonempty schema with no page entries returns the page-table empty InvalidInput. Holes and parent fields are represented by the dense page-table contract; the writer does not add alignment padding. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:83-106; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

Statistics finish mutates builders before writing any statistics bytes. A debug assertion compares stats rows to the next batch ID. Every root is written recursively under batch0 in a separate table; the field list named leaf_field_ids actually comes from all preorder schema IDs, including struct roots. Original data field IDs are encoded as statistics root names; newly converted statistics-schema IDs index statistics pages. None/zero-row collector output omits metadata; errors propagate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-625; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:623-627; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:635-670)

ManifestProvider is a public static async hook accepting &mut dyn Writer and &Schema, returning Result<Option<usize>>. The caller writes dictionaries first and trusts the returned position. Table ManifestDescribing creates a V1 Manifest with no fragments, then calls do_write_manifest directly with no indices/transaction, so dictionaries are not written a second time. The test-only NotSelfDescribing returns None and writes nothing. Metadata serialization maps None to zero; it is not an on-disk option-presence bit. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:35-64; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:639-650; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-250; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-75)

finish uses shutdown's authoritative size and the last cumulative row count, returning FileWriteSummary. It does not call tell afterward or retain other object identity fields. finish_with_metadata extends schema metadata first; both it and add_metadata overwrite duplicate keys. Failed/repeated finish is not locally guarded, and stats/dictionary/schema/footer side effects are not rolled back. No local abort or deletion follows cancellation; underlying Writer behavior remains a separate dependency. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:238-290; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-651)

## Preparation and ownership

prepare_indices runs tagged admission before cloning, derives physically rewritten columns and only then decodes/uses lineage if necessary; it preserves originals for coverage comparison. Supplied decoded ledger supports external history, while this method itself does no history IO. PreparedIndices binds only optional numeric manifest version. build_manifest_prepared checks that version, repeats admission and consumes original/prepared/reuse vectors. It does not bind source dataset identity or prove caller-supplied ledger/assembly correctness. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:466-535; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:593-624)

Convenience build_manifest supplies no read state; build_manifest_with_read_version prepares without ledger or settled FRI intent. External history rejection is conditional on actual rewrite decoding, not every operation on a tagged table. Normal dataset IO prepare_attempt loads current indices, and for Update with modified fields or Merge/DataReplacement loads first tagged ledger before calling preparation. This is a contextual caller excerpt, not complete retry analysis. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:540-590; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1570-1614)

## Finalization ordering and boundaries

After dispatch: stable-sort fragments by ID without deduplication; prune all-tombstone base files; reject overlay order violations; validate spilled carriers. Derive MemWAL catchup only if original list contained system metadata. Promote legacy blob schema roots referenced by V2_2/V2_3 files; choose Manifest constructor/default storage; set tag, optional auto flags, covering flags, sticky flags, timestamp and max fragment ID. Apply operation config/field metadata; range conversion; base additions; reservation; transaction path and next-row watermark; paired tagged flags; return. Later errors discard local candidate, not mutate current manifest. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1627-2025)

Config has distinct effects: existing stable reader flag keeps allocation active even when use_stable_row_ids=false, but RewriteRows index reuse additionally requires config true. Explicit storage_format wins over use_legacy_format; on an existing dataset only Overwrite applies requested default locally. disable_transaction_file influences feature derivation but final transaction_file is always Some supplied path. Primary/clustering guards reject reserved-key touches on established keys even if unchanged; only primary-key install calls schema verification. ## Failure and performance considerations

Local allocations include cloned manifest/index/fragment vectors, coverage bitmaps, name/ID maps and sorted offset Vecs. Delete uses lookup maps; selected offset updates still linearly locate original physical_rows for each target. Range conversion compares raw byte-start pointers without dereference and skips same backing by fragment ID only when both manifests opt in; it decodes all other inline data and uses copy-on-write fragments. No unsafe block is present. Integer high-water increments and several u64-to-u32 casts are unchecked. Partial Update's fallback bound is1<<24, while overlay stamping delegates its own bounds to row-version helper. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:82-142; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:704-765; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:796-948; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1563-1596; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1969-2063)

InvalidInput/NotSupported errors guard prepared version, admission/migration, base declarations, replacement layouts, offset bounds, missing overlay targets and key edits; helper errors propagate from decoding, row-version operations and validation. Restore awaits can be cancelled before returning owned state; main builder is synchronous, borrows current metadata and mutates owned candidates, with no global lock or CAS. Panics include unreachable Restore and inherited helper unwrap assumptions; debug_assert on stable Rewrite rewritten_indices is not a release rejection. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:168-217; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:495-687; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:917-948; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1090-1123; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1301-1562; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1887-2007)

Contextual normal/detached callers overwrite manifest.version, migrate metadata, fix schema, check storage/fragment IDs, migrate indices, withdraw narrowed catchup, then invoke write_manifest_file. Detached supplies no read state and chooses a random high-bit version; normal supplies read_version_state. This closes the immediate caller handoff only: full outcome verification, conflict rebase, retry and byte-write semantics remain pending. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1333-1411; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1832-1923)

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table persisted metadata contracts for fragments, data/overlay/deletion files, row lineage, and fragment-tree routing and mutations. It defines state and ordering rules, with no executable mutation or reader implementation. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:1-455)

## Complete range analysis

### Lines 1-7

SPDX license and ownership, proto3 syntax, and lance.table package establish the schema without imports. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:1-7)

### Lines 8-33

DataFragment groups column files for the same rows. Missing schema columns within a fragment read as all-null. id=1 is dataset-unique, files=2 is the file list, deletion_file=3 identifies tombstones, and overlays=11 must be empty unless manifest flag 64 is set. The overlay list is ordered: later entries win ties in committed_version for the same cell. The inline-tombstone bitmap question is a TODO, not an implemented arm. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-33)

### Lines 34-53

row_id_sequence holds serialized RowIdSequence bytes inline_row_ids=5, or an empty RowLineageColumn marker column_row_ids=12 referring to a file field -3. Row IDs follow physical row order, including unsorted example [1,42,3]. The comments say current writers keep inline bytes regardless of size. Any column arm requires manifest spilled-lineage flag 2048; otherwise an older reader could see an unset oneof and falsely infer no row IDs. This is a schema contract; current writer behavior still needs source confirmation. Empty marker declaration: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-53)

### Lines 54-73

last_updated_at_version_sequence uses inline bytes=7 or column marker=13 with reserved field ID -5. created_at_version_sequence uses inline bytes=9 or marker=14 with field ID -4. Both comments say current writers store inline regardless of size, and both column variants share the 2048 gate. Shared feature-bit requirement: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:54-73)

### Lines 74-89

Former external byte-range arms reserve numeric tags 6,8,10 and the three external_* names. The comment says no Lance writer ever emitted them and column arms replaced the design; do not interpret these reservations as readable active fields. physical_rows=4 counts original rows including deleted rows; logical count subtracts deletion_file.num_deleted_rows. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-89)

### Lines 90-125

DataFile.path=1 is dataset-relative. fields=2 lists signed field IDs: in-memory -1 is unassigned and must not persist; -2 is tombstoned; all negatives are reserved system values rather than schema fields and projection skips them, including -3/-4/-5 lineage IDs. The v1 comment assigns IDs by file position plus existing maximum and counts nested struct/list fields but one ID for a fixed-size list; v1 IDs are sorted but need not be contiguous. For v2 the field ID cannot determine the physical column because encoding choices change column count, so use column_indices. The example's wording about second fragments versus files is retained as a comment-level account, not confirmed allocator behavior. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:90-125)

### Lines 126-170

column_indices=3 is empty for v1, otherwise parallels fields exactly. -1 marks a field without its own top-level column; every other column index must be unique. The packed-struct/list/FSL example maps nine fields to [0,-1,-1,1,3,4,5,6,7], illustrating packed children and optional FSL structural columns. file_major_version=4 and file_minor_version=5 record file version; both zero identify historical 0.1 or 0.2 and do not uniquely choose one. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:126-170)

### Lines 171-184

file_size_bytes=6 supplies known disk length for fast footer lookup; zero means unknown rather than a known empty file. Optional base_id=7 refers to Manifest.base_paths for imported/referenced files. Presence must survive serialization; this declaration does not fully define absence resolution. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:171-184)

### Lines 185-221

DataOverlayFile stores replacement cell values without rewriting base files. Consult overlays newest to oldest, falling through to base when absent; deletions take precedence and suppress overlay values. data_file=1 contains one value column per declared field, no row-offset key column. Value position equals the count of coverage bits below the physical offset (zero-based rank), and columns can differ in length. coverage selects shared_offset_bitmap bytes=2 (32-bit Roaring offsets shared by every field) or FieldCoverage=4 (independent field offsets). Dense UPDATE and sparse MERGE are motivating examples, not different file types. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:185-221)

### Lines 222-239

committed_version=3 is the commit that made the overlay effective, not its read version. It is stamped at commit and restamped on retry. An index built at dataset_version >= committed_version incorporates the overlay; an older index must exclude affected cells for those fields and reevaluate current values. Greater committed_version wins across overlays; equal versions use later DataFragment.overlays position. Incorrect stamping or sorting changes query results. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:222-239)

### Lines 240-250

FieldCoverage.offset_bitmaps=1 is a repeated bytes list with one 32-bit Roaring bitmap per data_file.fields entry in the same order. A present offset whose value is NULL overrides to NULL; an absent offset falls through to base. A sparse NULL update must not be encoded by simply omitting the offset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:240-250)

### Lines 251-287

DeletionFile path is {root}/_deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{id}.{extension}. Nested DeletionFileType is ARROW_ARRAY=0 or BITMAP=1. Schema comments describe one Arrow IPC batch with an Int32Array column and .arrow, or Roaring bitmap and .bin. The current Rust implementation instead requires row_id:UInt32; this source/comment discrepancy is explicit in rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-34 and rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:162-195. Comments motivate sparse versus dense selection but provide no threshold. Fields are file_type=1, read_version=2, concurrent-writer differentiating id=3, num_deleted_rows=4, and optional base_id=7 for Manifest.base_paths. Deletions operate on offsets, not stable logical IDs. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:251-287)

### Lines 288-306

RowLineageColumn is an empty marker. Exactly one DataFragment.files entry carries the relevant reserved field ID (-3 row ID, -4 creation version, -5 update version), and its column_indices identifies the column. It may share a data file or be separate; values are non-null uint64, exactly physical_rows long in physical order. Only v2 data files support this mapping; v1 datasets keep sequences inline. Metadata is stored once in files, not repeated in the marker. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-306)

### Lines 307-323

ExternalFile is a table-relative path=1 plus byte offset=2 and size=3, documented for fragment reuse index details rather than the removed external lineage arms. FragmentTreeMetadata.layout currently has one tree=1 alternative; it selects the fragment storage layout. Removed external lineage arms: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-81. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:307-323)

### Lines 324-349

FragmentTree selects inline_root=1 or root_uuid bytes=2. UUID must be exactly 16 display-order bytes and resolves to _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root under this dataset. mutations_since_root=3 carries mutations absent from that root; next_action_sequence=4 is the next unused sequence for this version. FragmentTreeRoot stores children=1, buffer=2, and next_action_sequence=3 meaning the first action not represented by the root. Confusing root and version watermarks risks replaying or skipping mutations. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:324-349)

### Lines 350-391

FragmentTreeChild routing is ordered by min_key and owns [min_key,next min_key), with the final upper bound inherited. path=1 is relative to resolved dataset; optional base_id=2 inherits the containing object's dataset when absent and otherwise matches Manifest.base_paths, including valid ID zero. min_key=3 need not exist in the child. num_keys=4, total_rows=7, and visible_rows=10 include the object's buffered mutations; height=5 counts edges to leaves, num_children=6 direct children, both zero for leaves; object_size=8 is stored byte length. materialized_through_action_sequence=9 records a leaf's fully applied watermark with no qualifying mutations above it, zero meaning none; interiors must use zero. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:350-391)

### Lines 392-406

FragmentTreeNode holds children=1 and buffered mutations=2. FragmentTreeMutation holds action_sequence=1, FragmentAction action=2, and signed after-minus-before aggregate deltas fragment_count_delta=3, total_rows_delta=4, visible_rows_delta=5. Signed deltas preserve removals and deletions; these are validated changes by contract, not validation code. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:392-406)

### Lines 407-421

FragmentAction.action oneof selects complete upsert_fragment=1, remove_fragment ID=2, AddDataFile=3, RemoveDataFile=4, AddDeletionFile=5, ClearDeletionFile=6, or ReplaceDataFile=7. Upsert replaces the entire fragment and covers changes lacking narrower actions, including overlays, version sequences, and row IDs. Treating it as a partial patch would retain obsolete state. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:407-421)

### Lines 422-442

AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:422-442)

### Lines 443-455

ReplaceDataFile carries frag_id=1, expected_path=2, path=3, file_size_bytes=4, optional base_id=5. Replace only the first expected-path match, changing path/size/base while retaining column mapping and file version. An absent base inherits the dataset resolved for the tree object or version manifest containing the mutation; present base matches Manifest.base_paths. This differs deliberately from RemoveDataFile's all-match rule. Supporting all-match rule: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:428-432. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:443-455)

## Interaction and interpretation limits

This schema supplies file/tree state and explicit ordering invariants (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-455). It does not demonstrate actual reader/writer support, transaction conflict handling, tree balancing, mutation validation, or format stability of each feature. The inline-writer comments and column-arm definitions coexist; support must be traced rather than equating declared fields with emitted files (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81).

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table contracts for dataset manifests, index metadata, fragment-reuse mappings, and MemWAL shard/index state. This is a broad persisted-state schema; it records conflict-sensitive metadata but does not execute commits, recovery, fencing, or index catch-up. (protos/table.proto:1-769)

## Complete range analysis

SPDX, proto3, lance.table, imports of Any, Timestamp and file.proto, and public import of fragment_metadata.proto establish type visibility. The public import makes the separated fragment definitions accessible through table.proto rather than redeclaring them. (protos/table.proto:1-12)

### Lines 13-35

The opening historical-looking layout diagram lists encoded chunks, indices, chunk-position matrix, optional manifest, metadata, i64 metadata position, version pair and LANC. It is not the newer file2 footer diagram and should not be applied to every current file. UUID is a message with bytes uuid=1 documented as exactly 16 bytes; no validation is implemented in protobuf. (protos/table.proto:13-35)

Auxiliary data is version-specific, not inherited, and not loaded by default on query. (protos/table.proto:36-60)

Nested WriterVersion stores library string=1, version string=2, optional prerelease string=3, optional build_metadata string=4. Version is a string because library versions may not be semver; semver has no leading v. New manifests should store core major.minor.patch in version and separate prerelease/build to remain parseable by older readers. Absent prerelease leaves version as-is, absent build means none. Manifest.writer_version=13 enables detection of files affected by writer-specific bugs; this is not itself a file-format gate. (protos/table.proto:61-106)

reader_feature_flags uint64 tag 9 requires rejection when any set bit is unrecognized. The comment lists bit 0 deletions, 1 stable row IDs, 2 deprecated v2 indicator, 3 table config, 4 multiple bases, 5 disabled transaction-file writes, 6 overlays, 7 covering columns. Without bit 13, covering columns are the trailing fields suffix. Both readers and writers must reject unknown covering semantics to avoid querying/maintaining an index as if merely carried columns were indexed keys. (protos/table.proto:116-139)

Bit 8 enables mixed recognized exact v2 data-file versions, paired in reader/writer flags and one-way; use each DataFile version rather than snapshot default for decoding. Bit 9 combines stable row IDs and a fragment reuse index. Bit 12 means fragment-tree records and empty fragments. Bit 13 independently declares key fields versus covering_fields; it requires bit 7 in both words, and both bits persist even after dropping the final covering index. One field may appear in both lists. Enabling bit 13 reinterprets every index entry, so normalize all legacy entries atomically (or enable only when none covers), retain the bit in descendants until an atomic reverse conversion. The list omits bit 11 although fragment_metadata separately documents spilled lineage at 2048; do not treat this comment as exhaustive (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51). (protos/table.proto:140-161)

## Interaction and interpretation limits

This document analyzes every schema line, not the algorithms alluded to in those comments. Current feature support, stable/unstable designation, commit conflict matrices, writer fencing, recovery listing, and catch-up/cleanup safety require Rust source.
