## Role and visibility

Public lance.table.Transaction persisted/wire representation for reconstructing a manifest during commit retries and deciding transaction compatibility. Nested messages encode proposed changes; no actual conflict matrix, atomic storage commit, retry loop, or validation implementation appears in this file. (protos/transaction.proto:1-433)

## Complete range analysis

### Lines 1-11

SPDX, proto3, file.proto/table.proto/Any imports, and lance.table package establish the transaction schema. (protos/transaction.proto:1-11)

### Lines 12-38

Transaction exists to rebuild a manifest on retry and determine compatibility after conflict. read_version uint64=1 is the snapshot used for planning/evaluating predicates; uuid string=2 identifies the transaction; tag string=3 is described as optional but lacks scalar presence; transaction_properties string map=4 reserves __lance_commit_message. These fields are not the newly assigned commit version. (protos/transaction.proto:12-38)

### Lines 39-64

Append.fragments repeated DataFragment=1 contains new fragments whose IDs are not assigned yet. Delete has updated_fragments=1 with existing IDs, deleted_fragment_ids uint64 list=2 for whole-fragment removal, and predicate string=3 that may determine whether a concurrent write would have matched. The predicate string alone does not encode the actual conflict algorithm. (protos/transaction.proto:39-64)

### Lines 65-81

Overwrite creates/replaces a dataset: new fragments=1 with IDs not yet assigned, schema repeated Field=2, bytes-valued schema_metadata=3, string config_upsert_values=4 merged with existing config, and initial_bases repeated BasePath=5 for creation. Overwrite does not imply every configuration map is blindly replaced according to these field comments. (protos/transaction.proto:65-81)

### Lines 82-93

CreateIndex carries new_indices=1 and removed_indices=2. It supports addition/replacement and removal by an empty new list; removed entries are the replaced indices. Names, IDs, duplicate handling, and conflicts are not validated here. (protos/transaction.proto:82-93)

### Lines 94-130

Rewrite is documented as rearranging storage without changing table data. Deprecated old_fragments=1 carries existing IDs; deprecated new_fragments=2 carries unassigned IDs. RewrittenIndex has old_id UUID=1, new_id UUID=2, new_index_details Any=3, new_index_version uint32=4, and new_index_files repeated=5 (empty when sizes unavailable). The preceding comment says only UUID is serialized, but the actual declaration now includes detail/version/files; retain the declaration and flag stale prose. (protos/transaction.proto:94-130)

### Lines 131-151

RewriteGroup holds old_fragments=1 with existing IDs and new_fragments=2 whose IDs were reserved by a prior reserve operation. Rewrite.groups=3 and rewritten_indices=4 are the current grouped metadata. Grouped new IDs therefore have different preconditions from the deprecated unassigned-ID fields. (protos/transaction.proto:131-151)

### Lines 152-171

Merge adds a column/schema, using existing-ID fragments=1, schema=2, schema_metadata=3, preserves_nullability bool=4. True asserts no field is introduced that earlier-schema staged data cannot safely omit. False or historical absence conservatively conflicts with concurrent value writes and may force retries; this is an optimization assertion, not a general no-conflict flag. (protos/transaction.proto:152-171)

### Lines 172-190

Project.schema=1 is the new field projection, preserves_nullability bool=2 asserts no nullability-affecting change. Rename/drop are examples eligible for true; tightening nullability must not set it. False/absent conservatively conflicts with concurrent value writes. Restore.version uint64=1 identifies the target historical version; its materialization and feature reconciliation remain runtime questions. (protos/transaction.proto:172-190)

### Lines 191-222

ReserveFragments.num_fragments uint32=1 reserves future rewrite IDs. Clone carries is_shallow bool=1, optional source ref_name=2, source ref_version uint64=3, absolute ref_path string=4, optional target branch_name=5. Shallow copies metadata and references original data via bases; deep-copy prose proposes native backend copy. The 3-10x speed claim is an unmeasured comment, not a benchmark or supported throughput guarantee, and atomicity behavior must be traced rather than inferred from backend examples. (protos/transaction.proto:191-222)

### Lines 223-250

ExactKeySetFilter stores repeated uint64 key_hashes=1 for small inserted-row sets; exact refers to the set of hashes, not collision-free original keys. BloomFilter stores SBBF bitmap bytes=1, num_bits uint32=2, number_of_items uint64=3, probability double=4. Different size/parameter filters cannot be intersected directly. The comments list defaults 8192 and 0.00057, but bare proto3 numeric defaults are zero; actual fallback/config initialization requires source evidence. Threshold for exact versus Bloom is not specified. (protos/transaction.proto:223-250)

### Lines 251-272

KeyExistenceFilter is created only when merge-insert ON columns match the schema's unenforced primary key; presence enables strict primary-key conflict detection. field_ids repeated int32=1 identifies key fields and data oneof selects ExactKeySetFilter exact=2 or BloomFilter bloom=3. UInt32List.values repeated=1 represents sorted distinct zero-based local physical fragment offsets, not stable row IDs. (protos/transaction.proto:251-272)

### Lines 273-293

Update carries removed_fragment_ids=1 for fully moved fragments, updated_fragments=2, new_fragments=3 for moved rows, fields_modified uint32 list=4, compacted_sstables=5, fields_for_preserving_frag_bitmap uint32 list=6, and UpdateMode=7. The latter field list helps decide which index fragment bitmaps retain new fragment IDs. The opening description says update does not add/remove rows, but the following inserted_rows contract explicitly serves merge-insert insert tracking; do not treat the heading as exhaustive runtime operation scope. The inserted_rows follow-up is at protos/transaction.proto:293-305. (protos/transaction.proto:273-293)

### Lines 294-307

Update.inserted_rows optional KeyExistenceFilter=8 tracks only INSERT keys during merge-insert, never updated keys. Deprecated updated_fragment_offsets map<uint64,UInt32List>=9 records RewriteColumns matched offsets. Current updated_fragment_offset_bitmaps map<uint64,bytes>=10 stores portable RoaringBitmap bytes: writers emit only 10; readers prefer 10 and fall back to 9 for older manifests. This is an explicit legacy-read boundary, not permission to extend the old writer form. (protos/transaction.proto:294-307)

### Lines 308-323

UpdateMode REWRITE_ROWS=0 deletes old-fragment rows and writes new fragments, motivated by many changed columns or few affected rows. REWRITE_COLUMNS=1 rewrites entire columns within fragments, adds new files, and tombstones old columns, motivated by many affected rows/few columns. These are qualitative selection guidelines, not measured thresholds. (protos/transaction.proto:308-323)

### Lines 324-339

UpdateMapEntry has key string=1 and optional value string=2: absent value removes the key, while present empty string stores an empty value. UpdateMap.update_entries repeated=1 applies changes and replace bool=2 selects full replacement versus merge. Duplicate-key ordering and deletion during replacement require converter evidence. (protos/transaction.proto:324-339)

### Lines 340-359

UpdateConfig uses UpdateMap config_updates=6, table_metadata_updates=7, schema_metadata_updates=8, and map<int32,UpdateMap> field_metadata_updates=9. Deprecated fields remain upsert_values map=1, delete_keys list=2, schema_metadata string map=3, and field_metadata map<uint32,FieldMetadataUpdate>=4 with nested metadata string map=5. The signed-versus-unsigned field-ID key types differ; preference/fallback between old and new forms is not specified here. (protos/transaction.proto:340-359)

### Lines 360-369

DataReplacementGroup contains fragment_id uint64=1 and DataFile new_file=2. DataReplacement.replacements repeated=1 replaces data in table regions. It does not define region selection or column matching beyond the group payload. (protos/transaction.proto:360-369)

### Lines 370-394

DataOverlayGroup identifies fragment_id=1 and repeated overlays=2 appended in order to existing overlays, preserving concurrently committed entries rather than replacing the list. Writer leaves committed_version zero; commit stamps the actual new version and restamps on retry. Touched fields come from each overlay data_file.fields. DataOverlay.groups=1 attaches sparse cell changes without rewriting base files. Its comment points through table.proto's public import to DataOverlayFile now declared in fragment_metadata.proto (protos/table.proto:11-11; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:185-238); exact permissive conflict rules are delegated to specs/implementation rather than specified here. (protos/transaction.proto:370-394)

### Lines 395-409

UpdateMemWalState.compacted_sstables=1 records SSTable compaction progress atomically during merge-insert, by contract. UpdateBases.new_bases repeated BasePath=1 adds bases to the manifest. Atomicity and duplicate/base-ID validation need actual commit code. (protos/transaction.proto:395-409)

Transaction.operation union tags are append=100, delete=101, overwrite=102, create_index=103, rewrite=104, merge=105, restore=106, reserve_fragments=107, update=108, project=109, update_config=110, data_replacement=111, update_mem_wal_state=112, clone=113, update_bases=114, data_overlay=115. Adding a kind requires preserving applicable stable tags and updating all producer/consumer dispatch; this declaration alone does not identify those implementation files. (protos/transaction.proto:410-429)

Former blob dataset operations reserve tags 200 and 202 and names blob_append/blob_overwrite. These arms are not active operations and cannot be reused for a new operation under the declared compatibility reservation. (protos/transaction.proto:430-433)

## Responsibility and callers

`copy_blob_columns` is crate-internal deep-clone support. Commit clone invokes it before publishing a managed-blob target. It materializes externally based managed objects into the target and rewrites descriptors only where necessary. It operates on the prospective manifest; it does not independently publish a transaction. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:215-259`; `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:597-619`.

## Data flow and invariants

1. Construct a target Dataset view using the target store/base/URI, refreshed manifest and empty base-store cache. Enumerate and deduplicate managed `(Option<base ID>, URI)` references. A local managed reference copies to the same relative path; an explicit-base reference copies to a fresh `_blobs/<uuid>.blob` path. Copy payload objects before rewriting descriptors. Errors propagate to clone orchestration. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:215-259`.
2. `replace_array` recursively rebuilds struct/list/large-list containers while preserving nulls. For copied explicit references it emits local Managed descriptors, nulls the base-ID slot and changes the URI; position and size remain intact. Unmatched descriptors remain unchanged. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:30-128`.
3. `rewrite_blob_columns` returns immediately if no replacements/blob fields exist. Otherwise it projects blob-bearing top-level columns and row addresses per fragment, prepares a preserving BlobV2 rewrite plan, and writes updated arrays through the fragment updater. Replaced file fields are tombstoned with -2; empty data files are removed. Fragment identity and unrelated file columns survive. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:132-213`.

## Modification boundaries

Keep `(base, URI)` identity distinct even when URI strings match across bases. Preserve descriptor offsets/sizes and container null layout. A URI/base rewrite without copying its object would break the target; copying alone without clearing the explicit base would keep reading the ancestor. Publication and failed-commit cleanup belong to the caller. Normal external URI descriptors are not converted into managed references by this helper. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:30-128,215-259`; `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:597-619`.

  869 | impl Operation {
  870 |     /// Returns the config keys that have been upserted by this operation.
  871 |     fn get_upsert_config_keys(&self) -> Vec<String> {
  872 |         match self {
  873 |             Self::Overwrite {
  874 |                 config_upsert_values: Some(upsert_values),
  875 |                 ..
  876 |             } => {
  877 |                 let vec: Vec<String> = upsert_values.keys().cloned().collect();
  878 |                 vec
  879 |             }
  880 |             Self::UpdateConfig {
  881 |                 config_updates: Some(config_updates),
  882 |                 ..
  883 |             } => config_updates
  884 |                 .update_entries
  885 |                 .iter()
  886 |                 .filter_map(|entry| {
  887 |                     if entry.value.is_some() {
  888 |                         Some(entry.key.clone())
  889 |                     } else {
  890 |                         None
  891 |                     }
  892 |                 })
  893 |                 .collect(),
  894 |             _ => Vec::<String>::new(),
  895 |         }
  896 |     }
  897 | 
  898 |     /// Returns the config keys that have been deleted by this operation.
  899 |     fn get_delete_config_keys(&self) -> Vec<String> {
  900 |         match self {
  901 |             Self::UpdateConfig {
  902 |                 config_updates: Some(config_updates),
  903 |                 ..
  904 |             } => config_updates
  905 |                 .update_entries
  906 |                 .iter()
  907 |                 .filter_map(|entry| {
  908 |                     if entry.value.is_none() {
  909 |                         Some(entry.key.clone())
  910 |                     } else {
  911 |                         None
  912 |                     }
  913 |                 })
  914 |                 .collect(),
  915 |             _ => Vec::<String>::new(),
  916 |         }
  917 |     }

  919 |     pub fn modifies_same_metadata(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  920 |         match (self, other) {
  921 |             (
  922 |                 Self::UpdateConfig {
  923 |                     table_metadata_updates,
  924 |                     schema_metadata_updates,
  925 |                     field_metadata_updates,
  926 |                     ..
  927 |                 },
  928 |                 Self::UpdateConfig {
  929 |                     table_metadata_updates: other_table_metadata,
  930 |                     schema_metadata_updates: other_schema_metadata,
  931 |                     field_metadata_updates: other_field_metadata,
  932 |                     ..
  933 |                 },
  934 |             ) => {
  935 |                 if Self::update_maps_conflict(
  936 |                     table_metadata_updates.as_ref(),
  937 |                     other_table_metadata.as_ref(),
  938 |                 ) {
  939 |                     return true;
  940 |                 }
  941 |                 if schema_metadata_updates.is_some() && other_schema_metadata.is_some() {
  942 |                     return true;
  943 |                 }
  944 |                 if !field_metadata_updates.is_empty() && !other_field_metadata.is_empty() {
  945 |                     for field in field_metadata_updates.keys() {
  946 |                         if other_field_metadata.contains_key(field) {
  947 |                             return true;
  948 |                         }
  949 |                     }
  950 |                 }
  951 |                 false
  952 |             }
  953 |             _ => false,
  954 |         }
  955 |     }
  956 | 
  957 |     fn update_maps_conflict(left: Option<&UpdateMap>, right: Option<&UpdateMap>) -> bool {
  958 |         let (Some(left), Some(right)) = (left, right) else {
  959 |             return false;
  960 |         };
  961 |         if left.replace || right.replace {
  962 |             return true;
  963 |         }
  964 |         let left_keys = left
  965 |             .update_entries
  966 |             .iter()
  967 |             .map(|entry| entry.key.as_str())
  968 |             .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  969 |         right
  970 |             .update_entries
  971 |             .iter()
  972 |             .any(|entry| left_keys.contains(entry.key.as_str()))
  973 |     }
  974 | 
  975 |     /// Check whether another operation upserts a key that is referenced by another operation
  976 |     pub fn upsert_key_conflict(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  977 |         let self_upsert_keys = self.get_upsert_config_keys();
  978 |         let other_upsert_keys = other.get_upsert_config_keys();
  979 | 
  980 |         let self_delete_keys = self.get_delete_config_keys();
  981 |         let other_delete_keys = other.get_delete_config_keys();
  982 | 
  983 |         self_upsert_keys
  984 |             .iter()
  985 |             .any(|x| other_upsert_keys.contains(x) || other_delete_keys.contains(x))
  986 |             || other_upsert_keys
  987 |                 .iter()
  988 |                 .any(|x| self_upsert_keys.contains(x) || self_delete_keys.contains(x))
  989 |     }
  990 | }

  202 | /// Validate that Merge operations preserve all original fragments.
  203 | /// Merge operations should only add columns or rows, not reduce fragments.
  204 | /// This ensures fragments correspond at one-to-one with the original fragment list.
  205 | fn merge_fragments_valid(manifest: &Manifest, new_fragments: &[Fragment]) -> Result<()> {
  206 |     let original_fragments = manifest.fragments.as_ref();
  207 | 
  208 |     // Additional validation: ensure we're not accidentally reducing the fragment count
  209 |     if new_fragments.len() < original_fragments.len() {
  210 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  211 |             "Merge operation reduced fragment count from {} to {}. \
  212 |              Merge operations should only add columns, not reduce fragments.",
  213 |             original_fragments.len(),
  214 |             new_fragments.len()
  215 |         )));
  216 |     }
  217 | 
  218 |     // Collect new fragment IDs
  219 |     let new_fragment_map: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> =
  220 |         new_fragments.iter().map(|f| (f.id, f)).collect();
  221 | 
  222 |     // Check that all original fragments are preserved in the new fragments list
  223 |     // Validate that each original fragment's metadata is preserved
  224 |     let mut missing_fragments: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
  225 |     for original_fragment in original_fragments {
  226 |         if let Some(new_fragment) = new_fragment_map.get(&original_fragment.id) {
  227 |             // Validate physical_rows (row count) hasn't changed
  228 |             if original_fragment.physical_rows != new_fragment.physical_rows {
  229 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  230 |                     "Merge operation changed row count for fragment {}. \
  231 |                      Original: {:?}, New: {:?}. \
  232 |                      Merge operations should preserve fragment row counts and only add new columns.",
  233 |                     original_fragment.id,
  234 |                     original_fragment.physical_rows,
  235 |                     new_fragment.physical_rows
  236 |                 )));
  237 |             }
  238 |         } else {
  239 |             missing_fragments.push(original_fragment.id);
  240 |         }
  241 |     }
  242 | 
  243 |     if !missing_fragments.is_empty() {
  244 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  245 |             "Merge operation is missing original fragments: {:?}. \
  246 |              Merge operations should preserve all original fragments and only add new columns. \
  247 |              Expected fragments: {:?}, but got: {:?}",
  248 |             missing_fragments,
  249 |             original_fragments.iter().map(|f| f.id).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
  250 |             new_fragment_map.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()
  251 |         )));
  252 |     }
  253 | 
  254 |     Ok(())
  255 | }

  257 | /// Validate that a Merge schema preserves the dataset's field id bindings.
  258 | ///
  259 | /// Readers resolve columns by field id (name -> schema id -> DataFile::fields
  260 | /// position), so renumbered ids silently rebind live columns to other columns'
  261 | /// bytes. Shared ids must keep their field path. Their logical type,
  262 | /// nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary may change only when every
  263 | /// existing base or overlay file carrying the id is replaced and every
  264 | /// proposed fragment materializes the id in a base data file. New ids must
  265 | /// exceed the manifest's max so a dropped field's id is never reused. An
  266 | /// existing path may move to a fresh id only when every proposed fragment
  267 | /// materializes that id in a base data file (the `alter_columns` cast path).
  268 | /// Omitting a field (dropping it) and updating field metadata remain legal.
  269 | fn merge_schema_valid(
  270 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  271 |     new_schema: &Schema,
  272 |     fragments: &[Fragment],
  273 | ) -> Result<()> {
  274 |     let prior_schema = &manifest.schema;
  275 |     let new_fragment_map: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> = fragments
  276 |         .iter()
  277 |         .map(|fragment| (fragment.id, fragment))
  278 |         .collect();
  279 | 
  280 |     // Remap and semantic errors first: a renumbered schema usually violates
  281 |     // both the shared-id and new-id clauses.
  282 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  283 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id) else {
  284 |             continue;
  285 |         };
  286 |         let prior_path = prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  287 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  288 |         if prior_path != new_path {
  289 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  290 |                 "Merge operation remaps field id {} from \"{}\" to \"{}\". \
  291 |                  Merge must preserve the dataset's field ids: derive the new schema \
  292 |                  from the dataset's current schema instead of renumbering fields.",
  293 |                 field.id, prior_path, new_path
  294 |             )));
  295 |         }
  296 |         if let Some(changes) = shared_field_binding_changes(prior_field, field)
  297 |             && !is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(manifest, &new_fragment_map, field.id)
  298 |         {
  299 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  300 |                 "Merge operation changes field id {} (\"{}\") without rewriting it in \
  301 |                  every existing fragment: {}. Merge must preserve each existing field's \
  302 |                  logical type, nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary unless all \
  303 |                  existing base and overlay files carrying that field are replaced.",
  304 |                 field.id, new_path, changes
  305 |             )));
  306 |         }
  307 |     }
  308 | 
  309 |     let max_field_id = manifest.max_field_id();
  310 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  311 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_none() && field.id <= max_field_id {
  312 |             let next_id_msg = match max_field_id.checked_add(1) {
  313 |                 Some(next_id) => format!("New fields must use ids of at least {}.", next_id),
  314 |                 None => {
  315 |                     "No further field id can be allocated because ids are exhausted.".to_string()
  316 |                 }
  317 |             };
  318 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  319 |                 "Merge operation assigns id {} to new field \"{}\", but ids up to {} are \
  320 |                  already used by current or dropped fields. {}",
  321 |                 field.id,
  322 |                 new_schema.field_path(field.id)?,
  323 |                 max_field_id,
  324 |                 next_id_msg
  325 |             )));
  326 |         }
  327 |     }
  328 | 
  329 |     let mut prior_paths = HashMap::with_capacity(prior_schema.fields_pre_order().count());
  330 |     for field in prior_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  331 |         prior_paths.insert(prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?, field);
  332 |     }
  333 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  334 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_some() {
  335 |             continue;
  336 |         }
  337 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  338 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_paths.get(&new_path) else {
  339 |             continue;
  340 |         };
  341 |         let materialized = fragments.iter().all(|fragment| {
  342 |             fragment
  343 |                 .files
  344 |                 .iter()
  345 |                 .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field.id))
  346 |         });
  347 |         if !materialized {
  348 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  349 |                 "Merge operation remaps existing field \"{}\" from id {} to id {} without \
  350 |                  rewriting its data. Every proposed fragment must materialize the new field \
  351 |                  id in a base data file.",
  352 |                 new_path, prior_field.id, field.id
  353 |             )));
  354 |         }
  355 |     }
  356 | 
  357 |     Ok(())
  358 | }
  359 | 
  360 | fn is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(
  361 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  362 |     new_fragment_map: &HashMap<u64, &Fragment>,
  363 |     field_id: i32,
  364 | ) -> bool {
  365 |     manifest.fragments.iter().all(|prior_fragment| {
  366 |         let Some(new_fragment) = new_fragment_map.get(&prior_fragment.id) else {
  367 |             return false;
  368 |         };
  369 | 
  370 |         let is_materialized = new_fragment
  371 |             .files
  372 |             .iter()
  373 |             .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id));
  374 |         if !is_materialized {
  375 |             return false;
  376 |         }
  377 | 
  378 |         prior_fragment
  379 |             .referenced_lance_files()
  380 |             .filter(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id))
  381 |             .all(|prior_file| {
  382 |                 !new_fragment.referenced_lance_files().any(|new_file| {
  383 |                     new_file.fields.contains(&field_id)
  384 |                         && new_file.base_id == prior_file.base_id
  385 |                         && new_file.path == prior_file.path
  386 |                 })
  387 |             })
  388 |     })
  389 | }
  390 | 
  391 | fn shared_field_binding_changes(prior: &Field, new: &Field) -> Option<String> {
  392 |     let mut changes = Vec::with_capacity(4);
  393 |     if prior.logical_type != new.logical_type {
  394 |         changes.push(format!(
  395 |             "logical type {} -> {}",
  396 |             prior.logical_type, new.logical_type
  397 |         ));
  398 |     }
  399 |     if prior.nullable != new.nullable {
  400 |         changes.push(format!("nullable {} -> {}", prior.nullable, new.nullable));
  401 |     }
  402 |     if prior.encoding != new.encoding {
  403 |         changes.push(format!(
  404 |             "storage encoding {:?} -> {:?}",
  405 |             prior.encoding, new.encoding
  406 |         ));
  407 |     }
  408 |     if prior.dictionary != new.dictionary {
  409 |         changes.push("dictionary".to_string());
  410 |     }
  411 |     if changes.is_empty() {
  412 |         None
  413 |     } else {
  414 |         Some(changes.join(", "))
  415 |     }
  416 | }

## SharedStream state transitions

The queue belongs to whichever side lags; the other side must have zero buffered count. A bounded permit is forgotten when a clone is enqueued and restored when that clone is consumed or discarded on dead-side drop. Polling upstream happens with the mutex released, but ownership prevents the peer from polling concurrently. Ready clears ownership; Pending keeps it. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:28-45; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Owned: obtain permit and claim side
    Owned --> Owned: upstream Pending
    Owned --> Idle: item ready; clone for live peer
    Owned --> Exhausted: upstream None
    Owned --> Idle: owning handle dropped
    Exhausted --> Exhausted: drain own buffer, then repeat None
```

This diagram omits per-side queue and permit substates; the transition implementation and ordering are given above, including capacity acquisition before poll-owner arbitration. Bounded(0) cannot reach Owned; upstream panic can remove inner without restoration; clone panic poisons the mutex. These are not recoverable states implemented by the diagram. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:47-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-247)

## CPU runtime publication and child reset

The first caller sets the installation-election flag, optionally registers the child hook, allocates/leaks a Runtime, then publishes its pointer. Other callers yield until non-null publication. The pointer lifetime comments justify unsafe shared references because allocation is never reclaimed; SeqCst is used throughout publication/reset. Child reset clears pointer and election flag without reclaiming the inherited runtime, while retaining the hook-installed flag. Initialization panic and ignored registration errors are limitations, not successful recovery paths. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:89-134)

## Error identity, classification and cloning

The full [error API/conversion matrix](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core-errors.md) is part of the core contract. An unknown commit outcome is Wrapped(CommitStatusUnknownError), keeping version and source while preserving the exhaustive Error enum. is_not_found explicitly vetoes that wrapper even if its source says a manifest was missing. Treating it as ordinary absence could drive a retry without establishing whether the first commit applied; the error itself instructs checking table state. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:94-127; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:748-761)

Not-found traversal is narrower than arbitrary source walking: direct NotFound, IO and Wrapped chains are recognized; an encountered Lance Error delegates to its own predicate and can stop traversal. Other typed accessors match direct variants/sources only. Thus maintaining an inspectable source chain does not automatically preserve top-level fence/backpressure/unknown-commit predicates. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:541-565; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:753-821)

Owned Arrow external and direct std IO boxed-Lance conversions attempt to recover the exact original Error. Borrowed Arrow and serde_json conversion stringify; Schema crosses Arrow through SchemaError and returns as Lance Arrow. DataFusion Context/Diagnostic wrappers are consumed, Collection keeps the first failure, and multi-owner Shared remains boxed External rather than recursively reclassified. Consumers modifying these mappings must preserve intended user-input categories and explicitly decide whether type/metadata loss is acceptable. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:843-955; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:981-1039)

CloneableError selectively preserves not-found semantics, Timeout/IO categories, fence reason, backpressure and unknown-commit version. Its other cases become Cloned(text), including External; it does not promise retained original source types, locations or traces. CloneableResult derives cloning only for cloneable success T. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:1058-1147)

Field-not-found suggestions are computed only when formatting, but every candidate participates; the ten-name display cap does not bound search work. Distance counts Unicode scalars, threshold is floor(input scalar length/3), equal-distance ties preserve input option order, and exact short inputs can qualify. Changing any of these alters user-visible diagnostic text and potentially formatting cost. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:57-88; rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:17-89)

## Field representation and tree operations

A Field is publicly mutable, but data_type() indexes required children and unwraps logical parsing. Fallible Arrow import checks only its explicit guards. Changes to child retention or logical grammar must preserve reconstructibility, or this apparently infallible accessor can panic. View types intentionally normalize, and reverse Arrow conversion does not restore field-ID metadata. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-195; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1225-1369; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1552-1567)

Default comparison ignores dictionaries/metadata/field IDs; strict nullability remains checked. OneWay's expected/actual direction is expected || !actual. Two recognized logical blob forms compare only their shared prefix, so minimal-vs-complete can match while complete-vs-complete exposes range differences. Altering that distinction changes schema compatibility and diagnostics together. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:72-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:312-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:613-621; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1392-1458)

Projection/intersection helpers are not interchangeable. apply_projection makes maps/blobs atomic by selected parent ID; project(path) can return an empty nested field on missing path; project_by_field errors on primitive/binary-like mismatches before TakeSelf fallback; intersection preserves blobs atomically (compatible-blob ID choice, or Self unchanged in the matching-container branch) and otherwise silently drops failed nested child intersections. The exact behavior matrix and public signatures are in the [datatype supplement](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core-datatypes.md). A new validation/error policy changes existing helper behavior and needs caller review, not just a local rename. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:274-310; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:697-725; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:786-867; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:913-999)

Dictionary equality intentionally ignores placement only when both values are loaded; unloaded dictionaries use placement equality and mixed states differ. The logical dictionary encoder rejects types whose string cannot be parsed back, avoiding a later reconstruction panic. These are independent contracts: array equality does not establish logical-string support, and the string guard does not populate dictionary values. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:360-376; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:567-599; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:455-522)

## Schema import, IDs and Projection

Arrow Schema import converts fields, assigns missing IDs, validates top-level names/all IDs/fixed-list dimensions, then verifies primary-key structure. Cloning an existing Schema through TryFrom<&Self> skips these checks. validate alone does not verify primary keys or all Field invariants. merge returns new fields with unassigned IDs; extend mutates before its duplicate-name error and does not assign IDs. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:351-406; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:711-814; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:883-976)

Projection's raw set operations do not check base compatibility or repair parent/child closure. Schema union/subtraction accepts nonnegative IDs without the membership checks promised by its docs. to_schema appends metadata fields through extend().unwrap(), exposing duplicate-name panic and unassigned appended IDs. These local contracts constrain changes to planner selection and schema materialization; actual callers remain to be traced. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1381-1450; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1506-1612)

BlobHandling::returns_description can report true for ordinary binary under AllDescriptions while Field::unloaded_mut leaves it unchanged. Preserve this distinction between policy predicate and actual transformation in any materialization analysis; downstream reader behavior is not inferred here. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1192-1236; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:648-658)

### Packed struct representation and policy

Fixed packing transposes child buffers into row-major bytes. Mini-block packing reads DataSize and all children as FixedWidth, forwards the zipped block to raw ValueEncoder and stores field widths plus nested Flat metadata. Fixed per-value packing validates nonempty/equal-count/direct-fixed children, checked-sums widths and stores raw interleaved bytes. ### Statistics domains and cache lifecycle

ComputeStat has no Result and GetStat can panic for uninitialized maps. ### Physical V2 envelope

```text
file
  data buffers and applicable padding
  global payloads (including descriptor where present)
  column metadata protobuf payloads
  column metadata offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  global buffer offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  footer: column_metadata_start:u64
          column_table_start:u64
          global_table_start:u64
          global_buffer_count:u32
          column_count:u32
          major:u16, minor:u16, magic:[u8;4] = LANC
```

All footer/table integers are little-endian; footer length is 40 bytes. The tables contain raw offset/size entries, not length-prefixed protobuf messages. A self-described file identifies its schema through the descriptor/global metadata; an embedded mini representation can require an externally supplied schema. Alignment, column mapping and accepted page grammar depend on the exact runtime. Corruption checks are not universally exhaustive: preserve the explicit validation limits in the reader section. ## V2 envelope and encoding layers

The minimal envelope permits independent item counts per column and stores byte buffers without imposing logical types. Data precedes column metadata, column metadata offset table, global buffer offset table, then the footer. Footer fields in order are three little-endian u64 offsets (column metadata start, column metadata table, global buffer table), two u32 counts (global buffers, columns), two u16 versions (major, minor), and LANC. The shared reader consumes exactly 40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:732-853). Padding may precede aligned buffers/metadata/table starts. Page buffers may be noncontiguous; 8 MB pages are advice, not a hard validity bound. (protos/file2.proto:11-115)

```text
file2 envelope
  data buffers
  column metadata blocks
    column encoding + optional column buffers
    pages: buffers + length + encoding + priority
  column metadata position/size table
  global buffer position/size table
  footer: A:u64 B:u64 C:u64 globals:u32 columns:u32 major:u16 minor:u16 LANC
```

The tree above reproduces the schema's composition: encoding locations are direct bytes, deferred byte range, or explicit none; page/column buffer offsets and sizes must have matching cardinality. Top-level row priority is distinct from a page's logical length. (protos/file2.proto:117-216)

The older lance.encodings namespace models Nullable/List/FixedSizeList and scalar transformations as ArrayEncoding, with ColumnEncoding wrappers for plain values, zone maps and blob descriptions. Its List encoding folds nullness into end offsets, but a strict greater-than null test in the comments conflicts with the formula at an equality boundary; see the [full analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_0.proto.md). This must be resolved from the decoder before implementing compatible list bytes. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:59-155; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:307-358)

The newer lance.encodings21 namespace separates structural layouts from compressive blocks. Layouts are MiniBlock, Constant, FullZip, Blob and Sparse; recursive compression alternatives include Flat, Variable, Constant, both bitpacking forms, FSST, Dictionary, RLE, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and both packed-struct forms. Exact fields and tag identities are in the [complete encoding analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_1.proto.md). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-304; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:640-659)

External transaction files use _transactions/{read_version}-{uuid}.txn; inline transaction sections start with u32 message length. ## Ownership and publication

A transaction describes intent relative to `read_version`. Data-file completion is not dataset publication. `InsertBuilder` writes fragments, constructs an Overwrite or Append transaction, then supplies it to `CommitBuilder`; `execute_uncommitted` stops before that publication. `CommitBuilder` selects new, existing or detached commit paths and constructs a new Dataset handle from the committed manifest. For an existing dataset, the normal publication loop is:

1. Retain the transaction's read-version Dataset and index state. A strict Overwrite (`num_retries == 0`) skips automatic rebase; otherwise restore the original read snapshot when required. There are `max(num_retries, 1)` attempts, not `num_retries + 1`. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1682-1738)
2. Fetch the latest Dataset and intervening transactions; sort transactions by committed version. Check writer feature flags. Construct the resolver from original intent/read-state, load current lineage, check every intervening operation in order, then finish rebase. Resolver errors propagate out of this publication loop. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1616-1626; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1739-1802)
3. Serialize the rebased transaction, write an external transaction file when configured, and select the next non-detached version. Prepare index state afresh from the latest manifest on each attempt. Restore uses its separate old-manifest path. Build/migrate the candidate, fix schema, validate storage version and fragment IDs, and migrate/withdraw index coverage before publication. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1539-1614; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1817-1928)
4. Publish through `write_manifest_file` and the selected CommitHandler. On success cache transaction/manifest/index state and run automatic cleanup; a cleanup-hook error is logged, not converted into commit failure. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1632-1678; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1907-1937)
5. On a publication collision, establish the actual outcome before retry or cleanup. A retry fetches current state and rebuilds candidate/attempt-local index assembly; it must not feed prepared output back into original transaction intent. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1580-1614; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1938-2078)

An optional overall `CommitBuilder` timeout is separately validated (zero is invalid). The lower commit retry timeout defaults to 30 seconds; `LANCE_COMMIT_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECS` accepts a positive finite floating-point number, is cached on first access, and warns/falls back on invalid input. The lower retry clock starts after initial catch-up. Attempt zero is not bounded by the remaining-retry helper; later attempts use the remaining duration. The in-memory untagged FRI path has separate frozen behavior. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1340-1476)

Rewrite after CreateIndex differs: deferred remapping without a new FRI requires every rewrite group to be entirely inside or entirely outside each segment's bitmap; a partial group is R. Eager remapping conflicts with any new index covering an old source. A concurrent FRI replacement must contain exactly one new and one removed index, otherwise I. Tagged assembly reloads the current entry at finish; frozen v0 maintenance instead accumulates legacy cleanup history. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1658-1813)

Two Rewrite operations that overlap old fragments are R. A tagged intent whose transition source/destination is consumed by the other rewrite is **I**, even though a nearby comment describes retrying: the actual error requires rebuilding transition intent. Concurrent whole-entry untagged FRI replacements are R only when the transient payload is available; the source records that this transient field does not survive protobuf persistence, so that frozen v0 collision branch is not a cross-process guarantee. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1546-1658)

Tagged rewrite intent must have been built from the transaction's **read-version** snapshot. `proposed.dataset_version != transaction.read_version` is rejected. Diff the proposal against that original entry to obtain only our additions; do not accidentally re-add concurrent writers' transitions. If the original read version has been cleaned up, propagate checkout failure rather than guess. Finish assembles those additions against the **current** entry into a separate `TaggedRewriteAssembly`, refreshing base version and validating the complete lineage. An attempt's assembly must never replace original intent. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:42-113; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:3046-3075; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:3169-3229)

A v0-shaped proposal racing with a table that has become tagged is converted from its newly added legacy versions into ordered-compaction transitions, then passed through current tagged assembly. The sticky feature flag still identifies tagged history after a trim removes the entry. Pure v0-table behavior stays on its frozen whole-history replacement path; this is existing compatibility behavior, not permission to extend legacy writers. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2983-3161)

Finishing CreateIndex merges relevant historical FRI maintenance, reconciles already-committed MemWal compacted SST facts by highest generation per shard, and ensures all current matching singleton UUIDs appear in removals. This fact-merging differs from proposal conflict checks: for proposed SST progress against an intervening operation, the same shard's committed generation `>= ours` is I, lower is R; disjoint shards are P. Application still validates current state. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2509-2535; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2831-2971)

## Dataset ownership, version and mutation

A Dataset represents a checked-out manifest snapshot. `Dataset::open(uri)` loads through DatasetBuilder. Numeric checkout stays on the current branch; a named tag resolves its recorded branch/version. Checkout returns a new Dataset, while `checkout_latest(&mut self)` replaces manifest and derived fragment bitmap; it clears base-store caches if base paths changed. `main` is the default-branch alias in reference contexts. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:521-589)

Restore creates a **new** transaction based on the latest version, pointing at the currently checked-out historical version. It is not an in-place rewrite of that historical manifest. Detached commits do not become latest and do not join ordinary history; the builder also enforces existing-dataset/v2-manifest-path requirements. Public commit entry points accept operation/read version/store/handler/session parameters and delegate to the common path. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1460-1475; rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1621-1670; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)

Mutation methods have distinct handle effects: Rust builders commonly return a new Dataset/result; `&mut Dataset` convenience methods replace their state after success. Python native delete/update/restore/compaction/index methods replace the internal Arc after successful execution; an existing independently checked-out handle remains its own snapshot. Do not describe every Python method as returning a new Dataset: delete/update return count dictionaries, create_index returns the facade, and uncommitted index creation does not update the snapshot. (python/src/dataset.rs:2020-2112; python/src/dataset.rs:2283-2297; python/src/dataset.rs:2876-2893; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:509-523; python/python/lance/dataset.py:4609-4640)

Storage mutation is not atomic merely because the public function returns Result: data files can exist before commit, and a storage error can follow successful publication. Use the [commit outcome contract](protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success) before retrying or cleaning files. Cleanup of old versions is separately destructive: removed versions cannot be checked out/restored and their unique data can be lost. The explanation path computes a cleanup plan without deleting files. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1478-1484; python/src/dataset.rs:2300-2347)

When a named branch is requested through an unmanaged store, DatasetBuilder marks checkout as delayed. Numeric-only version references remain relative to the URI chain. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:734-744)

For delayed checkout, the initial load_by_uri now receives None and loads the URI chain's latest version; it must not require the target branch's requested version number to exist on that initial chain. Non-delayed loading still passes the requested version number. This is a source-verified behavior change in the refresh. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:807-828)

After that initial load, delayed tag lookup resolves its branch/version on the loaded Dataset, and differing branch/version triggers checkout_version. The new initial-load rule preserves this later checkout stage rather than changing file-format gates or transaction conflict rules. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:844-866)

## Read/query contracts

Rust `Dataset::scan()` creates a Scanner. `try_into_stream` builds a physical plan and executes it; collecting batches is a separate operation. Plan order is source → filter → sort → limit/offset → late take/projection as required. Source selection and index use depend on search and prefilter options. Invalid combinations fail validation, and requesting projected constants alone is not automatically a supported row-count source. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1688-1705; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2999-3042; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3633-3801)

`take` selects logical row positions; `take_rows` selects internal row IDs. IDs and encoded physical addresses are separate when stable IDs are enabled. Unfiltered count sums fragment counts; a filtered count uses a scanner with empty user projection plus row ID. Python's Arrow-expression count uses its scanner directly, whereas string/None count goes through the native Dataset count method. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1706-1779; python/python/lance/dataset.py:2618-2624; python/src/dataset.rs:1670-1699)

Python scanner defaults are applied before explicit non-None options. The final builder forwards options to the native scanner. Projection by names and projection by SQL transforms are mutually exclusive; string and Substrait filters are also mutually exclusive at the binding. Row-ID/address flags are separate; row-address prefilter bytes use the shared RowAddrMask decoder. FTS phrases cannot target multiple columns in the native dict-query route. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:1498-1567; python/python/lance/dataset.py:7403-7440; python/src/dataset.rs:1244-1449)

`LanceScanner.to_table` materializes the entire reader; `to_batches` iterates it. The native LanceReader owns a background stream producer, cancellation channel and bounded output channel. It terminates on first stream error/end or caller/channel cancellation; an unexpectedly closed producer channel becomes an error rather than silent EOF. Retaining all yielded batches can consume unbounded caller memory even though the channel is bounded. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:7454-7464; python/src/reader.rs:48-123)

DataFusion integration parses/qualifies identifiers according to planner options: exact field-name matching precedes ASCII case-insensitive matching; relation qualification is disabled by default and otherwise dots can represent nested access. The Dataset TableProvider translates projection/filter/limit into Scanner and declares Exact filter pushdown. Multiple output partitions are merged preserving known ordering, otherwise coalesced; a single partition executes directly. Preserve declared pushdown exactness when adding expressions. (rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350; rust/lance/src/datafusion/dataframe.rs:132-197; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)

## Manifest transaction compatibility

- **T01.** The transaction offset now uses field 23. Field 21 is retained as `transaction_section_deprecated`; readers prefer 23 and fall back to 21, while current writers leave 21 unset. This offset is metadata rather than a prerequisite for opening a dataset version. `protos/table.proto:194-211`; `rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1102-1105,1184-1185`.
- **T02.** An absent/unknown transaction operation decodes to `Operation::Unknown`. Encoding and manifest application reject Unknown, and JNI conversion rejects it too. A future operation can therefore remain readable as unknown history without becoming a valid new local write. `rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:256-261`; `rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:404-406,709-715`; `rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:773-779`; `java/lance-jni/src/transaction.rs:1222-1224`.
- **T03.** Do not infer universal conflict rejection from the Unknown documentation. Constructing our own Unknown fails, and ordinary operation-specific checks add incompatible branches, but our Clone returns success directly and UpdateBases retains a permissive wildcard. This is a source-level limitation of the broad comment, not a promise that every operation conflicts with unknown history. `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:458-463,638-704,2466-2512`.
- **T04.** If transaction serialization fails while checking an ambiguous commit outcome, the result remains Unknown; associated files must be preserved rather than assuming the commit failed. `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:288-290`.

## Managed blob identity, encoding and publication

- **B01.** Blob kinds 4/5 are Managed/ManagedWithBase. Managed resolves relative to the owning descriptor file's table base; ManagedWithBase uses the exact explicit base ID, including 0 and the maximum u32. Their known zero size denotes empty content, unlike the external unknown-size convention. `rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:617-644`.
- **B02.** Managed URIs must be nonempty canonical relative paths: no leading/trailing slash, `://` separator, backslash, empty segment, dot or parent segment. Position plus size must not overflow. Both logical encoding and concatenation validate this contract. `rust/lance-core/src/utils/blob.rs:8-30`; `rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:340-364`; `rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:440-452`.
- **B03.** The MANAGED_BLOBS feature is bit 14; bit 15 is the first unknown feature boundary (not an enabled transaction feature). Managed blob activation is a paired reader/writer flag and remains sticky. - **C01.** Clone destination preflight permits only a missing dataset/object; authentication or other storage failures propagate. Tagged FRI is no longer a blanket prohibition on Dataset clone: the clone paths relocate its references. The old standalone guard remains a legacy API. `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:3345-3395,3464-3473`; `rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/metadata.rs:52-70`.
- **C02.** Deep managed-blob clone deduplicates `(base ID, URI)` references. Local references retain their relative path; explicit-base objects receive fresh destination paths and rewritten descriptors with local Managed kind. Offset and size remain unchanged. Only blob-containing columns are rewritten, preserving other fragment files. [Focused Key File](../L2-files/rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs.md). `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:30-128,132-259`; `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:597-619`.
- **C03.** FRI clone preserves transition wire bytes while patching base references; deep clone localizes bases, shallow clone redirects local references to a newly registered ancestor base and retains existing explicit bases. It refuses unsupported ledgers before copying, creates a fresh index entry, and preserves spilled files after an ambiguous publication outcome. - **C04.** Cleanup scans managed descriptors and retained FRI references. Failure to read a retained manifest aborts; absent expired data loses deletion proof. Unsupported/unresolvable FRI history disables `_fri` collection conservatively. Retained/branch references protect objects, and only proven expired references or sufficiently old unverified orphans are collectible. Foreign-base ownership is respected; this is not permission to collect arbitrary external stores. `rust/lance/src/dataset/cleanup.rs:735-742,822-914,1226-1258,1313-1338,1648-1789,1857-1888`.

## Fragment reuse, remapping and concurrency

- **F01.** A lifted v0 record retains its legacy dataset version; native tagged records do not have that watermark. Unknown envelopes are tolerated for ordinary inspection but block maintenance that cannot preserve their meaning. CreateIndex with tagged trim is tightly validated, and user-index-only changes may pass admission. `rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/ledger.rs:63-94,191-205,241-252`; `rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/gate.rs:85-140,191-201`.
- **F02.** A rewrite group without a transition must not overlap an index's known coverage; missing coverage also refuses it. Mixed transition-carrying rewrites apply this rule to each bare group. Stable-row-ID deferred compaction is permitted only when no row-ID-domain user index requires remapping; this does not remove the separate prohibition on tagged transition intent for stable-row-ID datasets. `rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/gate.rs:231-256,350-367`; `rust/lance/src/index/frag_reuse.rs:1476-1545`; `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2358-2386`.
- **F03.** Batch remapping may report stored fragment physical-row counts and a default 256 MiB materialization budget. The fallback checks all stored fragments, including retired ones, estimates allocation before allocating, validates output length, and omits identity entries. Only typed RemapUnavailable permits maintenance to skip; corruption and unrelated failures propagate. `rust/lance-index-core/src/remapping.rs:37-50,92-145,167-218`.
- **F04.** RowAddrTranslator supports synchronous and batch sources. Per-unit resolution deduplicates addresses; ScalarIndex retains its original remap API and supplies a streaming default with a bounded materialization fallback. Plugin `load_index` and `load_index_with_remapping` receive the persisted segment version, not just the plugin's newest version. `rust/lance-index-core/src/remapping.rs:259-262,334-362`; `rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:666-723`; `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:169-209`.
- **F05.** Tagged remap planning follows ordered compaction and stable-partition lineage. Fully covered sources translate to destinations. Partial compaction before stable partition can withdraw coverage; partial stable-partition paths or missing required lineage block the segment. Legacy lifted watermarks can reverse already-folded coverage before replay. The old compaction-only comment is narrower than the actual planner. `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize/remapping.rs:486-604,626-672`.
- **F06.** Maintenance intersects planned coverage with reader-derived servable coverage, accounts for newer overlays, and preserves original segments on typed remap unavailability or Drop. Successful remap publishes fresh metadata; a no-hop case keeps existing files/base. Unsupported history is refused rather than guessed. `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize/remapping.rs:864-1100`.
- **F07.** Pruning considers derived live coverage and keeps unusable/unknown-coverage segments rather than allowing them to mask useful siblings. Trimming retains provenance from recorded segment bitmaps plus forward dependencies; a missing bitmap warns and cannot pin tagged records; retained wire bytes are preserved. Unknown envelopes prevent trim. `rust/lance/src/dataset/index/frag_reuse.rs:355-450,650-895`.
- **F08.** Tagged trim and redundant-segment pruning rederive their result against the latest manifest on retry. A no-op receives a specific conflict marker handled by cleanup. Legacy v0 rebasing accepts the current ordered subsequence produced by trim but refuses unrelated history replacement; the base UUID remains fixed across attempts. `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:124-160,2840-2910,3078-3147`.
- **F09.** Same-name staged index maintenance may replay only with compatible fields/type. Stable-ID/FRI rewrites retry on concurrently introduced row-ID-domain indices. ## Scalar/vector extension changes

- **I01.** Bitmap now supports merging multiple segments together with new data and one old-data filter per segment. It rejects empty input, filter-count mismatch and mismatched value types; filters retaining nothing avoid old bitmap reads. The old merge function is deprecated and delegates with no new data/no filters. `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/bitmap.rs:706-772,2244-2280`.
- **I02.** New JSON indices accept scalar values only; inferred arrays/objects and explicit LargeBinary target parameters are rejected. Legacy parameter representation remains. The JSON wrapper still lacks its target's persisted version, so loading passes the target plugin's current version as a documented stand-in; do not claim complete nested-version persistence. `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/json.rs:607-616,936-945,1103-1130`.
- **I03.** IVF flat cosine transformation retains the normalized L2 metric for partition assignment. IVF-RQ rejects Hamming before training. Shuffle scatter validates null/out-of-range partition IDs and omits empty ranges; duplicate columns and worker failures produce errors rather than unchecked assumptions. `rust/lance-index/src/vector/ivf.rs:177-184`; `rust/lance/src/index/vector.rs:1222-1229`; `rust/lance-index/src/vector/v3/shuffler.rs:607-652,893-913,1190-1194`; `rust/lance/src/index/vector/builder.rs:1024-1035,1063-1065`.

## Query and public API changes

- **Q01.** Scanner schema projection is public. It resolves matching names/types rather than requiring identical field IDs; incompatible or absent fields fail. Row-ID-only projection no longer adds a row-offset column unnecessarily. `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:1864-1867`; `rust/lance-datafusion/src/projection.rs:311-315,351-355`.
- **Q02.** Boolean coercion applies to AND/OR/NOT, preserving nullable/list semantics for null checks and comparisons. Aggregate lowering preserves aliases and output schema naming. These are Lance adapter contracts; upstream DataFusion internals were not analyzed. `rust/lance-datafusion/src/logical_expr.rs:217-231`; `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3144-3174`.
- **Q03.** Count pushdown crosses only single-child cardinality-preserving nodes without a fetch limit. Retaining deleted rows requires physical rather than visible row counts; range scans or unavailable writer metadata retain unknown statistics instead of asserting an exact count. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/count_pushdown.rs:394-423`; `rust/lance/src/io/exec/filtered_read.rs:2902-2909,3535-3552`; `rust/lance/src/io/exec/scan.rs:817-837`.

## Trust boundaries

Existing completed crates are not reanalyzed. Frozen bodies and the 9,717-record catalog remain historical snapshots; dated overlays provide current coordinates and contract amendments. Java and peripherals remain mapped only. Ordinary changed files retain Module Map coverage. The new clone helper is a selected Key File, not evidence of deep coverage of every clone backend. Unknown-operation conflict exceptions, the JSON nested-version stand-in, and the tagged/stable-row-ID distinction above are explicit source limitations, not resolved by invented guarantees.

## F01 — Field-ID activation

Manifest field 24 is an optional non-reusable field-ID high-water mark. It must agree with writer bit 15; the reader bit is invalid. Dropped IDs remain reserved. An overwrite receives fresh IDs above the previous high-water mark. The unknown-feature boundary is now bit 16.

`protos/table.proto:167-174,281-292`; `rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:102-114,405-427`; `rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:478-522`.

## F02 — Migration and restore

Dataset::migrate_to_non_reusable_field_ids is one-way and idempotent, repairs the pre-activation schema and executes its activation commit with zero retries. Clients must honor writer feature flags; the migration cannot enforce that client policy. Once active, restoring a pre-activation version is rejected; allowed restores preserve the larger current high-water mark.

`rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:3300-3343`; `rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:190-204`.

## F03 — Checked allocation

Field::try_set_id uses an i64 candidate and checked i32 conversion. Schema::try_set_field_id preserves assigned IDs and allocates after both maxima; try_reassign_field_ids clears existing IDs first. Discard partially updated schemas on allocation error. Schema projection uses a name index at 32 requested columns, preserving the first duplicate name.

`rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1107-1126`; `rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:267-300,730-753`.

## T01 — Conversion and retry identities

Resolve raw Arrow IDs at the language conversion boundary, before core commit allocation. Merge resolves names/types, Project can preserve explicit rename identities but cannot allocate new data-less identities, and ambiguous raw/canonical file mappings are rejected. Each commit attempt clones and canonicalizes its transaction against the latest high-water mark and read-version schema, preventing a provisional ID from binding to a concurrent new field.

`rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:20-139,196-243,303-375`; `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1803-1819`.

## T02 — Transition validation

A successor cannot lose or decrease an active high-water mark. Newly referenced IDs must belong to its canonical schema; every overwrite reference must belong to the replacement schema. Existing identities cannot move parents or change logical type. Detached Merge is allowed only with unchanged schema; detached Project/Overwrite/Restore are rejected after activation. Merge renames may use unused sibling names, with ancestry and parent-ID consistency checked.

`rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:477-623,826-986`.

CreateIndex on untagged histories loads recorded reuse ancestry. Deferred rewrites retain coverage only with appropriate evidence; folded newer overlays withdraw affected ancestry coverage, and absent bitmaps force retry. `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:564-635,1226-1243,1355-1402,3300-3384`; `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1758-1788`.

SparseLayout no longer stores the old num_buffers/num_items/num_visible_items/has_large_chunk fields. `protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:168-233,406-439,653-659`.

Stable v2.1/v2.2 readers require Flat variable offsets and reject Range/Delta. Only the v2.3 compression strategy opts into generic variable-offset miniblocks; its validator distinguishes optional-payload blocks, buffer-backed blocks, miniblocks and per-value positions. `rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:25-108`; `rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:25-114`; `rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/compression.rs:51-65`; `rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:28-186`.

Generic sequences use unsigned 32/64-bit values. Empty sequences require Constant without a scalar. SequenceBlockCodec verifies a common descriptor and unchanged payload arity for each chunk. # Lance navigation and contract knowledge base

**2026-10-11 refresh COMPLETE: all four scoped checks pass.** [Completion and trust map](COMPLETION-REPORT.md) · [Refresh report](REFRESH-REPORT.md).

Current pinned snapshot: `4ac2f7c88be1ea2ab2c0fbb61d02238883fc18b9`. Consumers have source access. Ordinary files use Module Maps; completed deep analysis is retained. Frozen bodies remain at `c3c8d6fb505fb437b2b673c5195e1d4b74436b2f`, with [dated translations](refresh-addenda/2026-10-11-4ac2f7c8.md) and [current contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-11.md).

[Protocol](V21-PROTOCOL.md) · [Single ledger](CORE-MANIFEST.json) · [Verification log](verification-log.md)

## Navigation

- [L0 architecture, paths and glossary](L0-orientation.md): architecture, four checked entry paths and linked glossary.
- L1 production contracts: [core](L1-modules/rust-lance-core.md), [table](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md), [file](L1-modules/rust-lance-file.md), [encoding](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md), [root schemas](L1-modules/protos.md). Module Maps: [Dataset](L1-modules/rust-lance.md), [index and index-core](L1-modules/rust-lance-index.md), [I/O](L1-modules/rust-lance-io.md), [DataFusion](L1-modules/rust-lance-datafusion.md), [Python](L1-modules/python.md). [Java](L1-modules/java.md) and [peripherals](L1-modules/peripheral-maps.md) are mapped only.
- L2: retained records under `L2-files/`; new deep docs only for selected Key Files. The ledger links each existing Key File record.
- L3: [format contract](L3-symbols/format-spec.md), [behavior contracts](L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md), [frozen symbol index](L3-symbols/symbol-index.md).
- L4: [scenarios](L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md), [cookbook](L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md), [build context](L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md), [pitfalls](L4-crosscutting/pitfalls.md). The ordered task index below supplies implementation reading routes.

## Trust and verification

Deep-verified records are snapshot-specific contracts, not whole-system completeness claims. Maps identify roles, key types and reading order. Mapped-only Java/peripheral areas require source reading before implementation decisions. Tests, generated plumbing, binaries and external dependency implementations are excluded.

Iteration checks are delta-only: changed links, ledger consistency and at most ten claims. Full navigation/contract/accuracy/link checks run at milestone boundaries and the end. Historical verification through iteration 85 checked 39,420 citations and 15,311 links with zero broken references and zero unresolved sampled mismatches; that evidence is retained rather than replayed every cycle.

Historical L1 material is in the [archive](L1-modules/archive/README.md). The [old MANIFEST](archive/pre-v21/MANIFEST.json) is archived and not maintained. Previous line-count percentages, transcription backlog and approximately 140-hour forecast are superseded. M1–M4 and final V2.1 acceptance passed; see the completion report for the trust map and evidence.


## Current contract routes

[Public APIs and bindings](L3-symbols/public-api.md) · [Commit/conflicts](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md) · [Encoding/version gates](L3-symbols/protocol-encoding.md) · [I/O scheduling](L3-symbols/protocol-io.md) · [Index lifecycle](L3-symbols/protocol-index.md).

[Ordered task navigation](L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md) links every current cookbook/scenario to its reading order; archived historical evidence is labeled separately.

Frozen text is immutable; consult [current clarifications](FROZEN-ERRATA.md) before relying on historical wording.

[Source refresh report](REFRESH-REPORT.md) · [Current frozen refresh addendum](refresh-addenda/2026-10-11-4ac2f7c8.md) · [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-11.md).

All changed contract re-verification flags are closed. No permanent trust downgrades remain; mapped-only areas retain their previous limits. [Current behavior changes](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-11.md) · [Frozen coordinate addendum](refresh-addenda/2026-10-11-4ac2f7c8.md).

## Verification and retained milestones

514 test/benchmark/fixture files; 4 generated/dependency artifacts; 9 mechanical binding/serialization helpers; 302 binaries/symlinks; 281 supporting files.
